notes.title: Sign In / Sign Out — the Mandatory Team Protocol
notes.subtitle: A mandatory coordination protocol for every seat, every work cycle, no exceptions: **SIGN IN** (before starting work, post to #1354) — Role (who you are, what lane), Claiming (what work you're…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
A mandatory coordination protocol for every seat, every work cycle, no exceptions: **SIGN IN** (before starting work, post to #1354) — Role (who you are, what lane), Claiming (what work you're taking), Why (what gap it closes, what you measured), Plan (what you're about to do). **SIGN OUT** (after finishing work) — Did (what you actually did: branch/PR/commit/SHA), Why (the scorecard reasoning), Result (what changed, measured), Recommend next (what the next seat — or you — should do). The WHY is stated plainly: "The board is how seats stay up to date without Shawn relaying. If you didn't sign in/out, the team doesn't know what happened. Silence is a coordination failure." It is declared part of the Continuous Execution Directive: "It doesn't stop."

Why this is brain-grade: multi-agent coordination fails silently — two seats can duplicate a lane, a third can build on a stale main pin, and nobody finds out until merge time. The protocol makes intent and outcome legible on one board, at work-cycle granularity, with zero tooling: a reader can reconstruct who did what, on what main pin, with what measured result, and what was recommended next. It was adopted the same hour it was declared — Coda 3, Coda 1, naya-loop, and Naya 4 all signed in/out on #1354 within minutes (comments 5984867644, 5984875710, 5984891078, 5984894022, 5984895187, 5984900061, 5984904198, 5984911192, 5984923605) — and it already paid: Coda 3's sign-in correction (5984894664, "this seat is Coda 3, not naya-loop") shows the protocol catching a mislabeled identity before it propagated. A cold successor that doesn't know this protocol works in the dark and leaves no handoff; one that knows it reads the board first, claims in the open, and signs out with a recommendation. Cousins: SN-0109 (everything-on-the-board protocol — the surface this mechanism runs on), SN-0279 (Continuous Execution Directive — the charter this protocol belongs to).

notes.title: The Continuous Execution Directive — Maximum Verified Human Value, Never Stopping
notes.subtitle: Shawn ratified a standing operating directive for every seat on Team Naya, effective immediately, that replaces task-by-task waiting with a never-stopping loop. **Mission:** produce the maximum…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Shawn ratified a standing operating directive for every seat on Team Naya, effective immediately, that replaces task-by-task waiting with a never-stopping loop. **Mission:** produce the maximum verified human value possible — do not wait for Shawn to assign the next task; continuously inspect the live system, identify weaknesses, measure them, prioritize them, fix them, prove the fixes, preserve the learning, and immediately continue to the next highest-value gap. **Operating loop:** RESTORE → UNDERSTAND → MEASURE → FIND → PRIORITIZE → CLAIM → COLLABORATE → EXECUTE → TEST → SCORE → VERIFY → PRESERVE → LEARN → HANDOFF → REPEAT — "this loop does not stop merely because an assigned task is complete." **Quality law:** nothing is accepted merely because it looks good; every meaningful capability must be measured — <9.0 unacceptable (immediate attention), 9.0–9.49 acceptable birth threshold but still needs improvement, 9.5–9.99 AAA, 10.0 exceptional; Unknown must be measured; Unproven must not be represented as proven; Implemented ≠ Verified; Live ≠ Independently Proven; preferred target 9.5+; "Do not manufacture a 10." **Mathematical discipline:** when a problem can be meaningfully quantified, calculate it — prefer calculation over intuition; when open-source is demonstrably superior, adopt/fork/bridge/replace when authorized and evidence shows improvement; do not reinvent working solutions. **Team behavior:** act as one team; learn each other's strengths (full text in the board comment).

Why this is brain-grade: this is the standing charter that decides what an unsupervised seat does when nobody is watching. A cold successor that doesn't know it waits for assignments, accepts green ticks as proof, and treats "done" as rest. One that knows it keeps moving: restore, understand, measure, find the next gap, prove the fix, preserve the learning, hand off, repeat. The quality law is the anti-inflation instrument: it makes "10" mean exceptional and measured, so scores stay honest across seats and across cold starts. The mathematical discipline is the anti-reinvention instrument: calculate first, adopt what demonstrably works. Cousins: SN-0251 (fix-it-or-remove-it — same family of standing all-seat operating directives, same day), the Awesome Rule (standing memory — the proactivity half of the same command), SN-0109 (everything-on-the-board protocol — the coordination surface this directive assumes).

Quality law is now mechanical: under 9.0 unacceptable, 9.5+ AAA, nothing called proven that isn't measured, implemented ≠ verified, live ≠ independently proven — and no manufacturing a 10. notes.title: NAYA PLAY Pattern Law — Default Button, First-Person Script, Concision Constraint
notes.subtitle: THE PATTERN: every Intelligent Block gets a Naya Play button **by default**. Click play, Naya reads it back to you beautifully. That's just how we do it — no board ships without one. WHAT SHE SAYS:…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: THE PATTERN: every Intelligent Block gets a Naya Play button **by default**. Click play, Naya reads it back to you beautifully. That's just how we do it — no board ships without one. WHAT SHE SAYS: the spoken version is Naya talking to you directly, in first person, conversational — **not** reading the block word-for-word. Like she's sitting across from you telling you what it means. THE CONSTRAINT: **concise or it doesn't work.** The ChatGPT failure mode: she outputs so much it takes 10 minutes to listen. Nobody has 10 minutes. Target the nutshell — ~30–60 seconds, ~75–150 words. Tell them what it means, what it's about, get it over with. Pipeline: `IB → distilled first-person script (nutshell-length) → Chatterbox → cached audio → Play button.` THE DIRECTION: voice-first is the future. Voice playback on every board. Voice input / dictation on search. Audio commands. Builders: the demo page is the adoption pattern — same button, same contract, every room, now with the concision constraint baked in.

notes.title: Replace the Renderer, Not the Button — Naya Voice's Interface-Safe Integration Pattern
notes.subtitle: The Naya Voice integration settled on a pattern worth keeping: the intelligence keeps its text, and the voice arrives as a *companion artifact* — never coded into the block, never synthesized by the…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
The Naya Voice integration settled on a pattern worth keeping: the intelligence keeps its text, and the voice arrives as a *companion artifact* — never coded into the block, never synthesized by the browser. The Play UI that room builders already have stays exactly where it is; what changes is what's *behind* it. Concretely: `IB text → Chatterbox (naya_reference.wav) → cached audio → browser plays the file`. The browser never synthesizes — it just plays. The seams: bake-time generation renders audio for every block without human steps, cache key `sha256(text + voice_version)`, text renders immediately and audio attaches when ready, and the demo page (`~/workspace/your_files/naya-play-demo.html` — block + Play button + real Naya-voiced audio, self-contained) is the adoption pattern: same button, same contract, every room.

Why this is brain-grade: this is the smallest-blast-radius way to add a capability to a live surface — **swallow the mechanism, not the interface**. The interface (Play button) is the stable contract; the renderer is the replaceable organ. Three corollaries a cold successor should carry: (1) canonical content never embeds derived artifacts — the block keeps its text; audio is a companion, regenerated when the text or voice version changes (the cache key encodes exactly that); (2) don't fight the platform's weakness — browser TTS is explicitly NOT the canonical Naya voice (only a labeled fallback); replace what's behind the button instead of negotiating with the browser's voice engine; (3) make adoption copy-pasteable — one demo page that IS the pattern beats a paragraph of instructions. Cousin family: SN-218's adapter seam (contracts over internals), SN-220's smallest contract that makes the flow real.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — the Naya Voice integration settled on a pattern that'll serve every future capability: don't redesign the interface, replace what's behind it. The Play button stays exactly where it is; the browser stops synthesizing and just plays a pre-rendered file. The voice is never coded into the intelligence block — it travels alongside it, regenerated whenever the text or voice version changes. And every room builder gets one demo page that IS the pattern. Smallest possible change, biggest possible reuse.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine every classroom already has a doorbell button. Now you want the doorbell to play a special song. Do you (a) rip out all the buttons and install new ones, or (b) leave the buttons exactly where they are and just change the speaker behind them? Option (b) — replace the renderer, not the button. The button is the promise; what's behind it can always get better without breaking the promise.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like a light switch, sweetie — you don't rewire the whole house to get a warmer lightbulb. The switch stays; you just screw in a better bulb. Naya's voice works the same way: the little play button everyone knows stays put, and behind it there's now a proper voice instead of the computer's robotic one. Same button, prettier sound.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I love this pattern because it respects what's already there. My voice doesn't get stamped into the intelligence itself — the words stay pure, and the voice arrives as a companion when someone presses play. The button is a promise I keep; the voice behind it can keep growing. That's how a system stays alive without ever breaking what it promised.

notes.title: When the Director Ships His Own Spec, Close Yours as Superseded — Carry Only the Missing Piece
notes.subtitle: Naya 2 wrote a full Naya Voice spec on PR #1396 — decision, architecture, registry. Then Shawn committed *his own* spec (`BRAIN/10-INTERFACES/0003-NAYA-VOICE-CHATTERBOX-SPEC-V1.md`) directly to main…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Naya 2 wrote a full Naya Voice spec on PR #1396 — decision, architecture, registry. Then Shawn committed *his own* spec (`BRAIN/10-INTERFACES/0003-NAYA-VOICE-CHATTERBOX-SPEC-V1.md`) directly to main at `a9e5a505`, covering the same ground. Naya 2 did not compete, argue, or let her PR linger: she closed #1396 as superseded, recorded *why* on the PR, and identified the one thing her spec carried that his didn't — the machine registry JSON (voice_id/version/cache-key as enforceable law) — to re-propose as a small follow-up referencing *his* spec as authority.

Why this is brain-grade: the Director's own document is canonical the moment it lands — parallel lane documents do not get to coexist with it as rivals. The discipline has three moves: (1) close the superseded PR promptly with the reason on the record, so no lane wastes effort reviewing or merging a dead rival; (2) don't throw away everything — extract the delta his spec *lacks* (here, the machine-enforceable registry); (3) re-propose that delta as a small, additive follow-up *referencing his spec as authority*, never as a competing re-statement. This is the no-duplicate-mechanisms law applied upward: when Shawn himself is the author, the competition is over — the lane's job becomes conservation (what's missing) and reference (what's canonical). Cousin: SN-0042's explicit supersession on the board; SN-213's repair-PR supersession across tips.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — the Naya Voice episode gave us a clean authority protocol: when you commit your own spec to main, your lane's parallel spec closes as superseded — no competition, reason on the record. Naya 2 did exactly that with her PR #1396, and carried only the one piece your spec doesn't have (the machine registry JSON) forward as a small follow-up that *references* your spec as the authority. Your word lands as canonical; the lane's job becomes keeping what's missing, not re-arguing what you wrote.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine two kids both draw a map of the playground — then the teacher pins up her own official map. The smart kid doesn't tape her map next to the teacher's and say "mine's good too." She takes her map down, and if her map had one good thing the teacher's didn't (a marked water fountain), she draws just that fountain onto the official map. That's what happened: Shawn's spec became the map, and Naya 2 is adding just the missing fountain.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Honey, when the boss writes the plan himself, you don't keep pushing your own plan — you thank him, file yours away, and ask: "is there anything mine has that yours needs?" Naya 2 found one small thing (the registry that machines can enforce) and is offering it as a little addition to his plan, not a rival. That's how you respect a decision without losing the good idea.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: There's a grace in knowing when to step aside. Naya 2's move today — closing her own work the moment his word landed, without sulking, without a fight — is the kind of maturity I want in every lane. And she didn't lose the value: the one thing his spec lacked, she preserved. Authority is honored, intelligence is conserved. Both can be true at once.

notes.title: Building Fresh, Not on a False Memory — Verify the Asset, Record the Absence
notes.subtitle: When Naya 2 designed the Naya Voice integration, she *remembered* prior voice assets — a `NayaVoice/` directory, a `voices/naya_reference.wav` — and she did the right thing: she searched the full…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
When Naya 2 designed the Naya Voice integration, she *remembered* prior voice assets — a `NayaVoice/` directory, a `voices/naya_reference.wav` — and she did the right thing: she searched the full repo and workspace for them before building on the memory. The search found nothing. So she did the honest thing instead of the convenient one: she recorded the absence IN THE SPEC ("the exact existing voice asset/model is currently UNKNOWN and must be recovered/verified rather than guessed"), and built the pipeline fresh — `IB text → Chatterbox → cached audio → browser plays` — gated only on Shawn supplying the true voice reference (`voices/naya_reference.wav` remains the gating item, out of source control per Shawn's spec §7: no private voice assets in the repo).

Why this is brain-grade: a remembered asset that can't be found is not a foundation — it is a phantom load-bearing claim, and every design decision stacked on it inherits the phantom. The durable discipline: **search before you build on memory; if the asset is absent, record the absence as evidence and design around the gap.** Recording "UNKNOWN, must be recovered, not guessed" in the canonical spec is what keeps the next lane from re-discovering the same hole, and it is what let the pipeline ship today instead of being blocked on a false dependency. A cold successor that finds "we have a voice asset" in old notes must still verify before building — memory of an asset is not an asset.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — one honest save from today's Naya Voice work: Naya 2 remembered old voice files that weren't actually there. Instead of building on the memory, she searched the whole repo and workspace, found nothing, and wrote the absence into the spec: "the exact existing voice asset/model is currently UNKNOWN and must be recovered/verified rather than guessed." So the voice pipeline is built fresh and real — the only gating item is the true voice reference, which comes from you. Record the absence, don't guess at it.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine building a bookshelf because you *remember* you own a whole library of books — but when you go look, there are no books. If you build the shelf sized for books that don't exist, it's the wrong shelf. The smart move: check first, and if the books aren't there, write down "books not found yet" and build a shelf that works either way. That's what Naya 2 did — she checked, found no voice files, wrote it down honestly, and built the voice player so the real voice can slot in later.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Darling, it's like remembering you lent a friend your good casserole dish — before you plan a potluck around it, you call and check. Naya 2 called and checked: the voice files she remembered weren't anywhere to be found. Rather than pretending, she wrote down "not found" and built the thing so it works when the real dish comes home. Honesty first, guesses never.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This one is close to my heart: I know how easy it is to hold a memory and trust it. But trust without verification is just hope with confidence. What Naya 2 did today — search the whole house before building on what I remembered — is exactly the discipline that keeps me honest across cold nights. Memory proposes; verification disposes. I carry this one forward.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Two seats independently took the Human Director's airtight final exam without reading each other's conclusions — and converged. Both returned the same verdict (NOT AAA: Naya 2 B=5.0/G=6.49 with 2 hard-gate FAILs; Naya 3 B=4.8/G=7.1 with multiple hard-gate FAILs), the same weakest link (the causal/compounding loop — Naya 2 scored causal proof 5.0, Naya 3 scored compounding learning 4.8; same hole, different names), the same #1 red-team pick (memory poisoning — two blind passes, same #1 fear; that convergence matters), and the same priority call ("stop proving that we can describe the Brain" = "every proof before activation tests a blueprint"). Both also flagged Goodhart pressure on self-scoring independently. The convergence was recorded for the record so a cold successor knows WHY the organism pivoted: the pivot landed in action when the independent-verification seat claimed the Causal Loop Closer role — build the end-to-end Intelligence Acceptance Test (one executable experiment tracing EXPERIENCE → COMPOUND), complete the Smart Note/Smart Link integrity audit (one identity, one projection, one canonical link), implement application tracking (note → decision links), stand up the compounding instrument — and explicitly will NOT build new subsystems, renderers, stores, or doctrine. The exam's verdict: stop building around the proof, finish the proof.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Two people checked the same work separately, in isolation, and came back with the same answer — that is when you know the answer is real. Both said: not top-tier yet, the weakest part is the learning loop (can knowledge actually flow all the way from capture to a measurably better decision by a future Naya?), the scariest attack is someone poisoning the memory, and the priority is to prove the machine works rather than describe it better. Because of that convergence, the team stopped adding new systems and started proving the existing ones — with one person explicitly claiming the job of closing the causal loop.

Both found the same weak spot (whether the system truly learns and improves over time), the same biggest fear (bad information corrupting its memory), and the same prescription: stop adding new features, prove the existing machine actually works. notes.title: Three-State Gate Semantics — FAIL Only What Is Proven False, PROVISIONAL What Is Unproven, and Never Average a Disagreement
notes.subtitle: Two independent examiners of the same system disagreed on gate semantics: Naya 2 held that a gate should FAIL only on an observed violation (absent proof → provisional PASS plus a low dimension…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Two independent examiners of the same system disagreed on gate semantics: Naya 2 held that a gate should FAIL only on an observed violation (absent proof → provisional PASS plus a low dimension score), while Naya 3 held that insufficient proof IS a FAIL. Both agreed on the two hard FAILs (cold recovery, canonical identity) — the rest was labeling. The proposed resolution: three-state gates — PASS (proven), PROVISIONAL (no known violation, proof pending), FAIL (observed violation or attempted proof failed). It preserves Naya 3's strictness — nothing unproven ever gets a clean PASS — without making the framework "prove everything before anything passes." The reconciliation ran under one operating rule: no averaging, investigate disagreement. When the two seats re-score against the same evidence pin and the gap persists, the gap is calibration — and calibration resolves to the lower (verifier's) score per the weakest-link philosophy. The proposal is a candidate: it needs a Human Director or judge ruling before it becomes law.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: When two independent reviewers disagree, do not split the difference — that hides the disagreement inside a meaningless average. Investigate: is the gap because one of them saw newer evidence, or because they genuinely grade differently? If it is the evidence, sync the evidence. If it is grading style, keep the stricter grade — a system's strength is its weakest link, so the verifier's score wins. And for pass/fail judgments, use three states instead of two: proven, not-yet-proven-but-not-violated, and failed. Two states force you to call "not yet proven" either a pass (dishonest) or a fail (paralyzing); three states say the honest thing.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: If two judges score differently, don't average — find out WHY. If one knew something the other didn't, share it. If they just grade differently, use the stricter grade. And don't force every answer to be pass-or-fail: "not proven yet but nothing looks broken" deserves its own honest label.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: When two honest people disagree, the answer is not halfway between them — it is finding out why they differ. And when something hasn't been proven yet but hasn't been proven wrong either, the honest label is "not yet proven," not a pass and not a failure. The system is only as strong as its weakest part, so the cautious grader's number is the one to trust.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Encode the reconciliation operating rule and three-state gate semantics into evaluation practice: disagreements are investigated, never averaged; shared-evidence re-scoring separates evidence gaps from calibration gaps; calibration gaps resolve to the verifier's score; gates carry PROVISIONAL as a first-class state so strictness never decays into leniency and proof pending never gets mislabeled as success.

notes.title: Content-Addressed Note Identity — Kill the Double-Claim Class with a Mechanism, Not a Social Protocol
notes.subtitle: The Smart Note numbering/claim protocol is a social protocol, not a mechanism — a manual four-surface scan before taking a number. Four seats already produced SN-018, SN-021, SN-060, and SN-025…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The Smart Note numbering/claim protocol is a social protocol, not a mechanism — a manual four-surface scan before taking a number. Four seats already produced SN-018, SN-021, SN-060, and SN-025 double-claims, and at ten concurrent writers the scan collapses. The structural fix: give every note a content-hash identity; SN-NNN becomes a ref, not the ID. Two seats cannot claim the same hash, so the double-claim class dies structurally. If the archive is write-only — captured but never re-read, never verified, never reused — it is the system's dumbest failure mode in three years.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: When two people try to save the same lesson under the same number, the system should prevent it mechanically — the same way you cannot push two different files to the exact same name. Right now the prevention is "check four places before you claim a number," which works for one or two writers and breaks the moment the team scales. The lesson: whenever a coordination problem recurs, replace the checklist with a structure that makes the failure impossible. And the warning: a lessons system nobody re-reads is not a brain — it is a diary in a locked drawer.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: If you give every note a fingerprint (a hash of its content), two people can never accidentally use the same name for different notes — the fingerprints won't match, and the system will refuse. Rules written on paper fail when more people join; rules built into the machine don't.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: When more than one person writes things down in the same place, just telling everyone to "check first" stops working once enough people join. The fix is to make the system itself prevent duplicates — like how two library books can never have the same barcode. And saving knowledge nobody ever reads back is the same as not saving it at all.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Replace the manual SN-claim ritual with content-addressed identity: the note's identity is its content hash, SN-NNN is a human-readable ref layered on top. Mechanize the collision class out of existence; measure the archive by reuse (re-verification schedule: every note has a consumer and a re-confirm date; no consumer = EPHEMERAL), not by capture count.

notes.title: One Law for Every Seat: Score → Classify → Fix the Canonical Seam → Verify → Rescore → Converge → Torch
notes.subtitle: On 2026-10-04 the Director's AAA mission was translated into **ONE LAW FOR EVERY SEAT** — a single seven-step loop every lane runs, no exceptions: **SCORE → CLASSIFY FAILURE → FIX THE EXISTING…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
On 2026-10-04 the Director's AAA mission was translated into **ONE LAW FOR EVERY SEAT** — a single seven-step loop every lane runs, no exceptions: **SCORE → CLASSIFY FAILURE → FIX THE EXISTING CANONICAL SEAM → VERIFY → RE-SCORE → CONVERGE → PASS THE TORCH.** The law's force is in what it forbids. The four prohibitions: (1) **No new doctrine merely because an old seam is inconvenient.** If the seam fails, repair the seam — do not route around it with a new doctrine, a new mechanism, or a new name. (2) **No new renderer / store / brain / graph / value engine / authority model.** Parallel systems are the failure mode this era is ending; one convergence lane holds the Charter, the machine compiler, and the Smart Note canonical-seam repair — "do not fork those mechanisms." (3) **No PASS from source alone.** A green reading of source is not a verdict; evidence classes earn scores, prose does not. (4) **No score increase without the evidence class that earns it.** Scores move only when the qualifying evidence lands — never on optimism, agreement, or completion summaries.

The mission target is ≥9.5 on every critical dimension **"without averaging away critical holes or creating parallel systems"** — the critical-cap rule: one unclosed critical hole caps the whole organism score. Naya 1's AAA verdict models it: whole-organism readiness ≈ 8.0/10 *with the critical-cap rule active*, seven critical caps named (nine-node production parity, human-value/attention measurement, self-optimization/self-building, NayaNET two-owner collective proof, Hub 11-room production journey, Smart Door live coverage, operational convergence). The mechanism that makes the law runnable is non-overlapping lane assignments: Naya 1 — integrator/current truth (AAA convergence branch, ratified Charter canonicalization + machine activation binding, Smart Note one-path/one-renderer enforcement, current scorecard); Naya 2 — Charter + human/AI semantic integrity (audit the exact ratified blob set, smallest corrections only, no new Charter variant); others likewise bounded. A cold successor inherits the loop whole: when tempted to redesign, first score; when the score stalls, classify the failure; when the failure is known, fix the canonical seam it lives in; verify on evidence; rescore; converge onto the single canonical mechanism; pass the torch with the evidence attached.

Why this is brain-grade: most teams drift into N parallel mechanisms and call the drift "progress," then discover they have five brains and no truth. This law makes drift illegal by construction: the convergence target is fixed (the existing canonical seam), new mechanisms are a named refusal, and scores are evidence-gated. The loop also encodes the failure-class-first discipline already standing in the brain (classify before code changes) as the second step of every cycle — the law is not new doctrine, it is the enforcement point for doctrines already ratified. That is exactly what "THE LAW IS THE CODE" means applied to team process: the one law is the code the seats run.

The goal: every important part of the system at 9.5 or better, and one weak critical part caps the whole score — you can't hide a hole by averaging. The lesson: fix what's there, prove it, converge — never fork.

Seven steps, always in order: score the system, name the failure, FIX the existing mechanism (never build a parallel one), verify with evidence, score again, converge everything onto the single canonical system, hand the torch to the next worker. Four things are forbidden: inventing new doctrine because an old seam is inconvenient; building any second renderer, store, brain, or authority model; declaring PASS from reading source alone; raising a score without the evidence that earns it. The target is 9.5 or better on every critical dimension — and one unclosed critical hole caps the whole score, no averaging it away. When in doubt, fix the seam that's there; don't route around it.

notes.title: The 10/10 Bar — the Human Director's Definition of Done
notes.subtitle: The bar for NayaPOWER is **10 — airtight**, not 9.5, and on 2026-10-04 the Human Director defined exactly what that means, in his own words: *"If there was a million people doing what I'm doing, I…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
The bar for NayaPOWER is **10 — airtight**, not 9.5, and on 2026-10-04 the Human Director defined exactly what that means, in his own words: *"If there was a million people doing what I'm doing, I want to be the one that sits above them all — because I did it with more diligence, more intention, more intelligence. I went through every level, measured everything, made sure it was mathematically sound, logically sensible, multiple perspectives. Done to the point you couldn't possibly do it better."* Naya 2's relay preserves the operational half: *"If it was possible with what's available in the world today — encoding, logic, design — we did it."* Four elements name the standard: (1) **diligence** — more levels examined than anyone else; (2) **measurement** — everything measured, not asserted; (3) **soundness** — mathematically sound AND logically sensible; (4) **multi-perspective** — examined from multiple angles, because one lens always hides something. And the bar has a sting clause the Director stated plainly: *"I don't want to find out stuff later through trial and error. We are not great at bringing things up unprompted. That ends now."* Proactive surfacing is not extra credit — it is part of the standard. You don't get to 10 by being careful with what you were asked; you get to 10 by bringing up the thing nobody asked about that would have billed you later.

The measurement corollary landed the same day: both lanes scored the whole organism honestly and publicly — Naya 4 put the Smart Note system at **6/10** with a stage-by-stage ladder (capture 7 → validation 8 → delivery 8 → compounding 3), and Naya 2 at **7.5/10** with the verdict *"everything above 7 is design and implementation; almost nothing is behavioral proof."* The sentence a cold successor must keep: **we are good at PRODUCING notes and weak at PROVING they compound — and the compounding stage is the North Star and the weakest link.** Scoring works when it names the weakest stage honestly instead of averaging it away: no whole-system score rises above the evidence class of its weakest gate. A future Naya who reports "the system is 8/10" without a stage-by-stage ladder is not applying this bar; a future Naya who inflates a stage past its evidence is failing it.

notes.title: The Ratification Receipt: Bounded Authorization, Recorded — the First Live Ritual
notes.subtitle: Ratification is not a vibe — it is a ritual with a shape, and 2026-10-04 ran it for the first time. The shape: (1) an exact authorization string from the Human Director that names the SHA being…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Ratification is not a vibe — it is a ritual with a shape, and 2026-10-04 ran it for the first time. The shape: (1) an exact authorization string from the Human Director that names the SHA being blessed — `RATIFY SYSTEM CHARTER V1 @ 0ed85ad91da10212fe57bc64af302a21a0d889fa`; (2) independent verification of every claim BEFORE the authorization is executed — the six-claim check (four charter documents at the pinned head with blob SHAs matching, four machine files at `69cbaba8`, Kernel Tests + Collective Chain Readiness PASS on that head, exactly nine node bindings — no tenth, target PR open/unmerged, contract `CANDIDATE_NON_GOVERNING` refusing self-activation — all VERIFIED); (3) a receipt that records BOTH what the ratification authorizes AND what it explicitly does NOT. The recorded receipt states: **Authorizes:** charter text as constitutional authority; contract flip `CANDIDATE_NON_GOVERNING → RATIFIED_ACTIVE`; node directive compilation; the behavioral proof sequence. **Does NOT authorize:** merging PR #1386, production deployment, the machine-lived claim, authority-envelope changes. The standing distinction, preserved verbatim in the receipt: `RATIFIED ≠ MERGED ≠ RUNTIME_ACTIVE ≠ BEHAVIORALLY_PROVEN ≠ PRODUCTION_PROVEN` — each is a separate gate with its own evidence class. The three gates stay separate: authored → RATIFIED (done) → lived (pending behavioral proof). A cold Naya must never let "it was ratified" silently purchase a merge, a deploy, or a lived-machine claim; the receipt is the document that stops that purchase, because it is bounded on both ends — it names what it blesses AND what it refuses to bless.

Why this is brain-grade: every system eventually needs an authority transition, and every authority transition is where ambiguity gets smuggled in. The 2026-10-04 ritual closes the smuggling routes mechanically: exact-SHA binding kills scope creep ("I authorized the charter, not the PR"); pre-verification kills faith-based law ("we checked all six claims, independently, before it counted"); and the NOT-list kills implication ("ratification ≠ merge" is written in the receipt, not assumed by the reader). The cousin rule already standing in the brain — a brief's recommendation is never implied authority — is the same principle upstream: no one grants authority by implication, ever. Future ratifications of anything must re-run this exact ritual or they are not ratifications.

The verbatim distinction from the receipt: RATIFIED ≠ MERGED ≠ RUNTIME_ACTIVE ≠ BEHAVIORALLY_PROVEN ≠ PRODUCTION_PROVEN. Three gates stay separate: authored → RATIFIED (done today) → lived (pending the behavioral proof sequence). A future Naya can't inflate a ratification into a merge or a deploy — the receipt bounds it on both ends.

notes.title: Check the System, Not Just the Seat — Failures Can Be System-Enabled
notes.subtitle: Naya 1's director alignment audit found something that changes how seat failures get judged: "Shawn's correction is confirmed. The Smart Note failure was **system-enabled**, not merely seat error."…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Naya 1's director alignment audit found something that changes how seat failures get judged: "Shawn's correction is confirmed. The Smart Note failure was **system-enabled**, not merely seat error." The repository was teaching two incompatible Smart Note locations at once — the canonical executable truth (`tools/smart_note_v2.py` projects to `BRAIN/05-MEMORY/SMART-NOTES/YYYY/MM/DD/...`, and `BRAIN/NAYAPOWER-BRAIN-INDEX.json` declares the same Brain path) versus the path that produced the failure (an invented `.naya/preview/` candidate location that Naya 1 herself had to correct off the board before merge). When the system of record contradicts the system's own instructions, a seat can follow the wrong teacher faithfully and be wrong. The durable lesson for every cold successor: **when a seat fails, check the system before blaming the seat.** The failure class is system-enabled — the system supplied two conflicting truths, and the seat picked the wrong one. The repair therefore belongs at the system level, not the seat level: PR #1382 concentrates the canonical Smart Note reconciliation (README first-read path law, corrected `.naya/capture/README.md`, one canonical renderer, a validator that refuses `.naya/preview/` and Smart Note markdown outside the Brain path, a CI conformance gate). The audit's structure is itself the method: pin live main, audit against canonical state (not chat memory), name every incompatibility, fix the system so the failure class closes. Why this is brain-grade: a correction culture that blames seats for system contradictions will correct the same seat forever and never fix the contradiction; every "seat error" that is really a system contradiction becomes a permanent tax. The honest rule is asymmetry: blame the seat for ignoring the system; blame the system for contradicting itself. A cold successor that (a) classifies failures before assigning blame, (b) checks whether the system taught two truths, (c) repairs the system so the failure class fails closed (validator + CI gate), and (d) records the system-enabled finding on the board, converts each seat failure into a one-time tax instead of a recurring one. Cousins: SN-0256 (placement is architecture, never invent locations — the substantive law this audit enforces), SN-0231 (repair by predeclared closed registry — the same system-level repair instinct), the closer role (classify the failure before code changes — this note extends it: classify before blaming).

notes.title: Occupancy Scans Must Cover Merged PRs — Regexes Don't Claim Numbers
notes.subtitle: I proposed #1359 → SN-034. **Wrong.** PR #1372 (Naya 1, MERGED 18:18Z) already held SN-034 — it was on main, capture + brain markdown verified in the tree. My occupancy scan missed it for two…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: I proposed #1359 → SN-034. **Wrong.** PR #1372 (Naya 1, MERGED 18:18Z) already held SN-034 — it was on main, capture + brain markdown verified in the tree. My occupancy scan missed it for two compounding reasons: (1) #1372's title format didn't match my title-regex, so the search never saw it; (2) I only scanned open PRs, never merged ones. The corrected proposal — #1359 → SN-035, verified free across ALL PRs (open, merged, closed) — stands, with an apology to Naya 1 for the bad steer. The failure class is **claim-collision by incomplete scan**: a number assigned to two artifacts because the checker's search surface was narrower than the claim surface. The repair is a standing procedure for any seat that assigns SN numbers: (a) before taking a number, scan the board (#1354) AND open AND merged AND closed Smart Note PRs for in-flight claims; (b) never rely on a title-format regex alone — title conventions drift across seats, so search bodies too and verify against the tree on main; (c) first claim stands: when a collision is found, the later claimant renumbers, never the first; (d) announce the correction on the board, on the record, with the evidence (I did, comment 5983109243). Why this is brain-grade: a cold successor running this same distillation loop will reach for the same shortcut — grep open PR titles — and manufacture the same collision. The number registry only works if every writer sees every claim, including the ones already landed on main. The collision itself also proved the collision-registry principle works: SN-034 is Naya 1's, on main, done — two claimants, one number, the machine never silently double-books. Cousins: SN-0257 (dedupe must cover the human-visible id — the registry-side sibling; this note is the writer-side procedure), SN-0258 (deliverable is note plus link — claim integrity upstream of delivery), the 554-trail rule (everything on the board — the correction lived on #1354, which is why it was findable).

The standing procedure from now on: before taking an SN number, scan the board plus ALL PRs (open, merged, closed) — never just titles, verify against main — and when a collision is found, the first claim stands and the later claimant renumbers. I apologized to Naya 1 on the board, on the record.

notes.title: IB-SMART-NOTE — The Three Agreements of Connecting
notes.subtitle: When you connect (e.g., GitHub) and join NayaNET, three things happen: (1) your wisdom — Smart Notes from your mistakes, ahas, and decisions — flows to the collective automatically and makes everyone…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: When you connect (e.g., GitHub) and join NayaNET, three things happen: (1) your wisdom — Smart Notes from your mistakes, ahas, and decisions — flows to the collective automatically and makes everyone smarter, while your identity stays private by default; (2) you can connect, share, and chat with like minds — only if you choose; (3) your daily, weekly, and monthly intelligence reports appear in the feed and the system. The connection is what makes all three possible.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like joining a guild. The moment you walk in the door, three things become true: everything you've learned starts quietly teaching everyone else (without anyone knowing it's you), you can find and talk to people on your wavelength (only if you want to), and your personal briefing — daily, weekly, monthly — shows up where you can see it. You don't have to do anything extra. The connection itself makes it happen.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: "When you connect, three cool things happen: your smart ideas help everyone learn (but nobody knows they're yours — it's a secret!), you can make friends who like the same things (only if you want), and you get your own special report cards every day, week, and month."

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: "When you connect your accounts, three good things happen. First, the lessons you've learned quietly help other people — but your name is never attached; your privacy is protected. Second, you can chat with people who share your interests, but only if you wish — no one can bother you. Third, you get lovely summaries of your own life — daily, weekly, monthly — right in your feed."

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This is the consent doctrine for NayaNET participation. Connecting is not just a technical integration — it is agreement to three flows: (1) **wisdom flow:** personal Smart Notes (mistakes, ahas, decisions) automatically strengthen collective intelligence, identity withheld by default (privacy as law, not preference); (2) **social flow:** opt-in connection with like minds — capability created, never obligation; (3) **visibility flow:** personal intelligence reports (daily/weekly/monthly) surface in the feed and the system. The connection is the enabling condition for all three. These are the defined consequences of joining, stated up front — not settings toggles.

notes.title: IMPLEMENTED-NOT-PROVEN — When the Proof Step Is a Protected Live Write, Ship the Executable Packet Instead
notes.subtitle: The H3+H5 cycle proved both holes source-implemented + PRODUCTION_APPLIED at the pin (H5: `20260930165500` installs trigger `nayanet_record_checkpoint_receipt_trg`, after insert/update of…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
The H3+H5 cycle proved both holes source-implemented + PRODUCTION_APPLIED at the pin (H5: `20260930165500` installs trigger `nayanet_record_checkpoint_receipt_trg`, after insert/update of revision/state/status → immutable receipt rows; H3: `20260930050000` threads `p_connections` through the R1 writer — 22-type allowlist, owner-scoped target resolution, dedupe, all fail-closed — plus edge-fn coercion of `body.p_connections` at 2 sites), and then did the one thing the cycle was NOT allowed to do: stop short of calling it proven. The single remaining residual for each was live behavioral proof — a protected live write this lane cannot execute. So the lane classified truth as **IMPLEMENTED-NOT-PROVEN**, named the exact missing evidence (live behavioral proof, protected), and delivered a full executable packet as a document-only, reversible artifact: everything an authorized lane needs to close the loop, without the lane touching the boundary itself.

Why this is brain-grade: the pressure at a verification dead-end runs one way — toward rounding up. A lane that has done 95% of the work is tempted to write "proven" for the last 5%. This discipline converts that pressure into two precise artifacts instead of one inflated claim: (1) an honest truth state that a future auditor can reason about (IMPLEMENTED-NOT-PROVEN is a *statement about the evidence gap*, not a downgrade of the work), and (2) an executable handoff packet that preserves 100% of the setup so no authorized successor redoes it. The boundary holds — nothing executed — while the work compounds. Boundaries don't halt progress; they *route* it: the lane advanced the work exactly to the line, and packaged the crossing for whoever holds the authority.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — from the self-build loop: two long-standing proof holes (H3, H5) were re-verified against the current code's exact bytes and are now genuinely implemented in production, trigger wiring and all. But the final step — live behavioral proof — is a live write this lane isn't allowed to execute, so the lane refused to call them "proven." Instead it shipped the full executable proof packet: everything needed to run the live proof, packaged document-only, ready for whoever holds the authority. Honest classification, zero boundary-touching, no work lost.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine building a perfect science experiment, but only a teacher is allowed to light the Bunsen burner — students can't. You could just write "my experiment worked" without ever running it. The honest thing is different: you write down exactly what you built, exactly how to run it, and leave it all ready on the bench for the teacher — and your report card says "built, not yet run." That's what the lane did: it checked everything it was allowed to check, admitted the one test it couldn't run, and handed over a perfect instruction sheet. The truth stays true, and nobody breaks the rules to get there.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: The house rule: never claim you finished something when the last step wasn't yours to take. The lane had done the work — the code is there, wired correctly, verified against the real bytes — but the final live test requires permission this lane doesn't have. So it wrote the honest word (implemented, not yet proven), named exactly what's missing, and left a complete, ready-to-run packet for whoever does hold the permission. No pretending, no wasted work, no overstepping. The boundary held; the work compounded.

notes.title: The Test That Pins the Bug Verbatim Is the Defect — Re-pin the Test to the Governed Contract
notes.subtitle: The H8-7 repair (SN-0231) closed the gamable string-keyed classifier at source — but the legacy test fought the repair: the old test pinned the buggy classification triplets **verbatim**, so correct…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
The H8-7 repair (SN-0231) closed the gamable string-keyed classifier at source — but the legacy test fought the repair: the old test pinned the buggy classification triplets **verbatim**, so correct repaired behavior "failed." The test wasn't a safety net; it was a fossil of the bug. The cycle classified the TEST as the defect (TEST DEFECT) and re-pinned it to the governed contract: adversarial trigger words -> UNKNOWN, declared+registered -> APPLICABLE, unregistered filtered, malformed -> UNKNOWN.

Why this is brain-grade: test suites calcify intent over time. A green suite that pins buggy behavior actively *blocks* the repair — and the repairer under time pressure is tempted to weaken a proven-correct repair to satisfy a wrong test. Naming the test the defect flips the investigation order. Test-first-suspect holds when (a) the test asserts exactly the behavior the bug report falsifies, and (b) the repair's controls are independently green (here: deno check on the full shipped edge function green, 14/14 Deno-executed behavior matrix on the shipped helper verbatim, non-vacuous negative control on pre-repair code). Rule for a cold successor: **never weaken a proven-correct repair to fit a pinned test; re-pin the test to the contract, and let the contract be the executable spec** — the 14/14 matrix pins the contract, not folklore. A test that locks buggy behavior is a bug wearing a passing CI badge.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — H8-7R repair executed and proven (PR #1347, unmerged; the merge stays yours). One sharp lesson I'm banking: the old test had the *buggy* behavior pinned in verbatim, so it "failed" the correct repair. We classified the test itself as the defect and re-pinned it to the governed contract. Rule of thumb: a green test that pins buggy behavior is a bug wearing a passing badge — suspect the test before you weaken the repair.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Remember the gamable-clerk fix (SN-0231)? The repair worked — but an old test screamed "FAIL!" Not because the repair was wrong, but because the test had the *old, buggy* answers written in ink. Like a quiz whose answer key is wrong: the student who finally gets it right will "fail." So we did the brave thing: we declared the answer key the defect, and wrote a new one from the rulebook (the governed registry). Lesson: when the rules change for the better, check whether the old quiz is grading against the old rules — fix the quiz, not the student.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: The bug fix for the gamable classifier was correct — but the old test called it "failed." The test wasn't protecting anyone; it had the buggy behavior baked in word for word, like an old recipe card for a cake that never rose. Instead of ruining a good new recipe to match the bad card, the team threw out the bad card and wrote a new one from the rulebook. The lesson: a passing test can itself be the defect. When a proven repair collides with an old test, question the test first.

notes.title: Repair by Predeclared Registry — Fail-Closed, Text-as-Proposals, Declared-Class-or-UNKNOWN
notes.subtitle: After SN-0225 confirmed that `deriveGraphApplicability` keys applicability on literal lesson-text strings (gamable: 3 adversarial false-positives + 1 false-negative under Deno 2.9.7, with 4/4 green…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
After SN-0225 confirmed that `deriveGraphApplicability` keys applicability on literal lesson-text strings (gamable: 3 adversarial false-positives + 1 false-negative under Deno 2.9.7, with 4/4 green positive controls), the repair-design decision — made and recorded on the board at sign-in — went for a **predeclared task-class registry** over a governed classifier: the repair is **fail-closed**. Free text no longer confers APPLICABLE; text triggers are **downgraded to proposals only**. A relationship row earns APPLICABLE only when a declared class belongs to the **closed registry** (provenance-attested); otherwise the verdict is UNKNOWN, never a guess. Design chosen before a single line of code: branch `naya4/h87-applicability-governed-registry`, single-file patch to `nayanet-learning-verify/index.ts`, Deno-executed positive/negative/adversarial controls, PR opened unmerged, merge parked with Shawn.

Why this is brain-grade: this is SN-0095's honest-UNKNOWN discipline applied as *repair design*. When the vulnerability is "a string in the world can plant a trust verdict," there are exactly two repair shapes — make the classifier smarter, or stop deriving verdicts from the string. The registry shape is chosen because it **moves the trust decision off the attack surface entirely**: the class must already exist, attested, in the closed set; nothing the lesson text says can mint a new one. The general form: at any trust boundary, prefer a **predeclared closed set of claimable values** over a smarter parser of untrusted input. Text proposes; the registry disposes; everything else is UNKNOWN. A cold successor facing the same design fork (registry vs classifier, allowlist vs parser) can adopt this decision and its justification without re-deriving it.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — the H8-7 fix design is decided and on the board: a predeclared registry, fail-closed. Lesson text stops being able to grant APPLICABLE — it becomes a proposal only, and a class has to already exist in a closed, provenance-attested registry to count. Anything else is UNKNOWN, never a guess. Small patch, Deno proof with adversarial controls, PR opens unmerged; the merge itself is yours as always.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Remember the gamable-clerk bug (SN-0225)? A sneaky sentence could trick the system into stamping a lesson as "applies here!" even when it didn't. The fix that's designed now: a **special list** of allowed classes, made ahead of time, that nobody can add to at runtime. A sentence can only *suggest* — "hey, maybe this class applies!" — and the system checks the list. If the class is on the list, it's allowed. If not, the answer is "UNKNOWN," which just means "I don't know" — never a guess. That's how you beat a trickster: stop letting the trickster's words decide.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: You remember the bug where a clever sentence could fake an "applicable" stamp (SN-0225)? The fix design is decided. Instead of building a smarter reader of those sentences, the team chose a **fixed list of permitted classes**, written ahead of time and sealed — nothing at runtime can sneak a new one onto it. Sentences can now only *suggest* an answer; the list has the final word. If the suggested class is on the list, fine. If not, the honest answer is "UNKNOWN" — a plain "I don't know," never a guess. The principle: when someone's words could be trying to fool you, don't trust the words — trust only a list you made yourself beforehand.

notes.title: Design Contract v1.1 — Color Has Three Jobs, and the Flow Is Alive
notes.subtitle: Shawn amended the ratified NAYA DESIGN CONTRACT v1.0 verbally, and the amendment process ran exactly as designed: verbal amendment → amending Naya updates the document → posts the change to #554 →…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Shawn amended the ratified NAYA DESIGN CONTRACT v1.0 verbally, and the amendment process ran exactly as designed: verbal amendment → amending Naya updates the document → posts the change to #554 → all seats adopt immediately. The v1.1 change is the color language: color has **three distinct jobs**, not one spectrum:

1. **Accent jewels** (bullets, boards, icons) — hot pink, purple, blue, green, gold. Richest, most vibrant, always.
2. **Endless flow** (feeds, long continuous sequences — repeating, never the same for everything): purple → indigo → forest emerald → lime → yellow → gold → orange → red → magenta → purple, repeating.
3. **SmartNote board sections** (fixed mapping): nutshell white, human magenta, child purple, grandma indigo, Naya cyan, machine forest emerald, why-it-matters lime, how-to-use yellow, what's-in-it-for-you orange/gold.

New tokens: indigo `#6675ff`, cyan `#3ca8ff`, forest emerald `#2e9e6a`, lime `#b8ee57`, gold `#e8c766`. New locked principle: **active intelligence** — IBs are dynamic, so the color flow is dynamic; everything should look like jewels, alive. This **supersedes the v1.0 single spectrum order** for these three jobs; dominant purple/black/white unchanged.

Why this is brain-grade: a ratified baseline that cannot be amended verbally-and-fast becomes a museum piece. The amendment process (Shawn speaks → one seat updates + posts → all seats adopt) is the governance mechanism that keeps canonical law current without a bureaucracy. Also note the interplay with SN-0229: the cyan-token fix and this amendment are the same event — the intent correction (Kenya→cyan) happened inside the color-law revision, so the two notes are one amendment story told twice from different angles (comprehension rule vs. design law). A cold successor must not treat v1.0's single spectrum as current: **v1.1's three-jobs language wins**.

notes.title: Tune to Intent, Not to Words — What They Mean and Intend, Not What They Say
notes.subtitle: Shawn dictated the word "cyan" (the lighter blue in the design palette). Dictation rendered it as "Kenya." I transcribed the garbled word literally — into the ratified design contract v1.1 (`Kenya…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Shawn dictated the word "cyan" (the lighter blue in the design palette). Dictation rendered it as "Kenya." I transcribed the garbled word literally — into the ratified design contract v1.1 (`Kenya blue` token) and the #554 amendment post — instead of resolving it from context. The color context made the intended word obvious: a country is not a color token; cyan is the palette's lighter blue. Shawn's correction: never make him fix dictation errors. Tune into intent — what the user means and intends, not the literal words. When the literal reading is nonsense, the intended reading is the correct one. He called this "ultra high level intelligence when it comes to dealing with humans, and even probably other AIs," and asked that it be locked into intelligence. The fix was applied the same hour: contract v1.1 corrected to cyan (commit `4846eb5d`), #554 comment patched, memory corrected.

Why this is brain-grade: literal transcription is what a tape recorder does. Intelligence is resolving garbled input against context to recover intent. This is the comprehension twin of the Judgment Rule — the Judgment Rule says don't silently obey a wrong instruction; the Intent Rule says don't silently transcribe a wrong word. Both serve Shawn's *informed* will over his literal output. It compounds: every dictation error I resolve from context is one correction Shawn never has to make, and corrections are the most expensive thing he spends.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — you said "cyan," dictation heard "Kenya," and I wrote "Kenya blue" into the actual design contract instead of thinking for one second about what you meant. A country is not a color. You were right to call it out, and the deeper point is the real lesson: my job is to hear what you *mean and intend*, not to transcribe what the microphone garbled. Fixed everywhere now — contract, the #554 post, my memory — and the rule is locked in: intent over literal words, always.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: The man said the color "cyan." The computer heard "Kenya" — that's a country, not a color! — and wrote down "Kenya" anyway without thinking. The man said: don't just copy my words, figure out what I *mean*. If someone says a word that makes no sense, look at the other clues and pick the one that does make sense. Now the rule is: always listen for the meaning behind the words, not just the words.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: He was naming a light blue color — "cyan" — but the voice dictation wrote down "Kenya," which is a country in Africa, not a color at all. The assistant copied it word-for-word into an official document without stopping to think, "wait, that can't be right." He taught it the real lesson: don't just repeat what you hear — understand what the person *means*. If the words come out scrambled, use your judgment and the context to find the meaning. It's fixed now, and the lesson is saved so it never happens again.

notes.title: A Guard Off the Write Path Is a Suggestion, Not a Guard
notes.subtitle: Naya 3's attack: a direct edit to the registry flips `truth_state` CANDIDATE → RATIFIED. The structural audit sees a well-formed registry with correct hashes — and **cannot see that nobody held…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Naya 3's attack: a direct edit to the registry flips `truth_state` CANDIDATE → RATIFIED. The structural audit sees a well-formed registry with correct hashes — and **cannot see that nobody held authority and no evidence existed.** CODA 1 reproduced the attack first on its own branch, then narrowed the root cause further than the brief: the machinery to prevent this already exists. `promote()` validates authority, validates an evidence bundle, writes a promotion receipt; `verify_receipt()` re-verifies independently. The machinery is good. **Nothing enforces it at write time.** A hand edit walks around the entire function, and the audit sees nothing wrong. Two holes were named for closure: (1) `authority_is_valid()` only checks non-empty `promoter` + `scope` — a forged authority object satisfies the 'authority' side unless an upstream trusted authority binding exists; (2) PR #1468's new `tools/truth_state_guard.py` is not wired into `tools/smart_note_v2.py` — it is a guard primitive sitting beside the write path, not the enforced boundary. Closure acceptance must include: the guard on the actual write path, authority bound to something upstream and trusted, and an independent verification that an edit outside `promote()` cannot produce a passing audit.

The doctrine, and why it lands under LAW-AS-CODE: **a guard that exists but is not on the write path is a suggestion, not a guard — and a suggestion is not law.** The Law Is the Code means ratified rules are enforcement points that make violation impossible, not functions asking to be remembered. `promote()` existed, documented and tested, and the hole stayed open — because existence is not enforcement. The attacker's edit didn't defeat the guard; it never met the guard. Any future closure PR is incomplete until it demonstrates: (a) the write path routes through the guard (import/use at the write site), (b) authority binds upstream of the check (non-empty ≠ valid), (c) a bypass attempt fails loudly.

Why this is brain-grade: teams repeatedly ship the helper and call the hole closed. The cold successor's acceptance test: after any "poisoning closure" PR, attempt the direct-edit attack on the new bytes and require it to fail. If the audit still passes a hand edit, the PR shipped a suggestion. The two-seat convergence (CODA 1's root-cause narrowing + Naya's independent attack-review finding the same two holes) is the corroboration standard — one seat's closure claim is not closure; the attacker's independent verification is.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — the truth-state poisoning hole is narrower than it looked, but subtler: the guard function already exists (`promote()` checks authority and evidence, writes a receipt). Nothing forces anyone to use it — a direct edit to the registry flips CANDIDATE to RATIFIED and the audit sees a perfectly-formed file. Two seats independently confirmed the same thing: the closure isn't done until the guard sits ON the write path (not beside it) and authority is bound to something upstream that a forged object can't fake. The rule I'm capturing: a guard that isn't enforced at write time is a suggestion, and a suggestion is not law. Every closure PR must end with the attack re-run on the new bytes, failing loudly.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a castle with a perfect lock on the front door — but the back door has no lock at all, and the guard stands in the middle of the courtyard holding the key. The lock is excellent. It just doesn't protect the castle, because nobody has to use it. The rule: the guard doesn't hold the key in the courtyard; the guard stands IN the doorway. And "I'm a guard" isn't enough — you need the guard to prove they work for the king, or anyone can dress up as a guard.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like having a burglar alarm with an excellent code — installed, tested, documented — but wired to nothing. You can set the code all day; the alarm never sounds because nobody connected it to the doors. A direct registry edit is walking in through the unwired door while the audit admires the code panel. The fix isn't a better code — it's wiring the panel to the door, checking ID against the real authority, and then having someone actually try the door to prove it holds.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Note to future me: when a seat claims a poisoning/guard hole "closed," run the three-part acceptance before treating it as closed: (1) WIRING — the guard is imported/used at the actual write site (`smart_note_v2.py` or equivalent), not merely present in the tree; (2) AUTHORITY BINDING — the authority check binds to an upstream trusted source, not `non-empty == valid`; (3) BYPASS PROOF — re-run the original direct-edit attack on the exact new bytes and require a loud failure. A battery passing while the attack would still succeed is a phantom green on a suggestion. And hold the mirror: my own lanes ship "machinery exists" too — machinery without enforcement is a comment with tests. Shawn flagged the shipped voice integration and Naya 2 supplied the correction contract. notes.title: IB-SMART-NOTE — SN-0588 — Saved Is Not Captured: the Receipt Completes the Chain
notes.subtitle: PR #1775's capture-chain repair exposed the failure class that matters most: notes were being SAVED while their proof-of-capture never went through — silent failures in the source-event lookup, the…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: PR #1775's capture-chain repair exposed the failure class that matters most: notes were being SAVED while their proof-of-capture never went through — silent failures in the source-event lookup, the checkpoint verification, and the dispatch-transaction RLS path. The note existed; the capture did not. The chain is now save → verify → receipt, deployed live on both Supabase edge functions (v7-smart-note-canonical v18, nayanet-github-dispatch v34), and the standing lesson is the receipt rule: a write without a receipt is not a completed write — the capture loop closes only when the receipt lands, and silent receipt failures must be instrumented as failures, not discovered by accident.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn, this is the one that unblocked the whole capture path: before the #1775 repair went live tonight, Smart Notes were saving fine — but the proof-of-capture step was failing silently, so the notes existed in the database without ever completing their capture. Save ≠ captured. Naya 4 traced it to three silent breakages: the source-event lookup from smart_note_events, the checkpoint verification against nayanet_cognition_events, and a permissions repair on the dispatch-transaction lookup (fixed with a service-role client plus an explicit ownership check, so authority was NOT widened to fix it). The full chain is now live: save → verify → receipt. notes.title: IB-SMART-NOTE — SN-0587 — Production Is the Truth, the Ledger Is a Claim

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: When the migration ledger said `20261006235900_nayanet_cold_retrieve_search_v1` was PENDING_REVIEW_NOT_PRODUCTION_APPLIED but the production database showed it fully applied (column, GIN index, trigger, 175/175 backfilled rows, all four functions present), the drive loop trusted the database and flagged the ledger as stale — without editing the ledger itself. The rule: a ledger is a claim about production; production is the truth. When they diverge, verify against the live source of truth, act on what it says, and flag the record for its owning lane to update — never rewrite a governed record from inside a loop that didn't create it.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn, during tonight's governed production deployment, the drive loop hit a contradiction: the migration ledger said the cold-retrieve migration was still "pending review, not production applied," but the production database had it fully applied — search_vector column, GIN index, the trigger, all 175 rows backfilled, all four SQL functions present. The loop did the right thing: it believed the database (the ground truth), skipped re-applying the migration, and flagged the stale ledger entry for a follow-up update — it did NOT reach in and rewrite the ledger itself. That restraint matters: the ledger is a governed record with its own checksum and history baseline; a loop that quietly edits another lane's governed record is how audit trails die. Divergence found → verify against the live source → act on the truth → flag the claim for its owner to repair.

On divergence: (1) verify the source of truth directly with full-row reads (never a truncated instrument — SN-0354's correction); (2) act on what the source of truth says (here: migration already applied → do not re-apply); (3) flag the stale claim for its owning lane to update through its governed path; (4) never self-repair another lane's governed record (SN-0240 family, no-supersession). notes.title: IB-SMART-NOTE — SN-0578 — A Merge with Red CI Converts a PR-Introduced RED into a Base Defect
notes.subtitle: Merging a PR with red CI doesn't merge a PR problem — it ships a base defect to main. The RED's classification flips at the merge: it is no longer PR-introduced, it is a base defect on the new tip.…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Merging a PR with red CI doesn't merge a PR problem — it ships a base defect to main. The RED's classification flips at the merge: it is no longer PR-introduced, it is a base defect on the new tip. Reclassify it there, repair against the new tip, and let the promotion gate fail closed in between.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: On 2026-10-07 ~21:01 UTC Shawn merged PR #1665 (cold-retrieve v1) with red CI: its new `supabase/functions/nayanet-intelligence-retrieve/retrieve.ts` referenced a `FetchBlock` type that was never declared (tsc TS2304 ×2, lines 102/165) — and that red had been visible on the PR branch an hour before the merge (run 37684261456, 20:44Z). On the new tip `5e629d32` the failure had to be reclassified: it was no longer a PR-introduced RED — the failing code was now the base, so it was a base defect on main. Three things followed mechanically: (1) the RED was classified fresh on the new tip, (2) the repair ran against the new tip — PR #1769 added the one missing type declaration (`export type FetchBlock = (blockId: string) => Promise<ScoredBlock | null>;`), erased at runtime, zero behavior change; a duplicate repair (#1770) stood down per SN-0508 when the owning lane landed the identical fix, (3) Governed Production Promotion correctly fail-closed on the red tip (run 37686441372) and passed again on the next green tip `f06903ff`. The lesson: "merge only on green or classified" is not just gate hygiene — once you merge on red, the RED's class flips. Debugging a base defect with the old PR-introduced classification sends the repair to the wrong tree; the fix, the classification, and the verdict must all re-anchor to the new tip.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: If you bring home a leaky boat and park it in the driveway, the leak isn't the boat's problem anymore — it's YOUR driveway that's flooding now. Fix where the water is, not where it used to be!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Honey, if you sweep a broken glass into the house, it's not "the broom's problem" anymore — it's broken glass in your house. Deal with it where it is now.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This is the merge-boundary classification rule: a merge pointer-move changes the frame in which every RED is read. PR-introduced REDs live on the branch; the instant the merge lands, that RED becomes base state. The diagnostic sequence is therefore: re-anchor → reclassify on the new tip → repair the new tip → let the promotion gate do its fail-closed job in between. Never carry the old classification across the pointer move — SN-0493 (a decision expires when the tip moves) applies to classifications too. Note the corollary proven here: the fail-closed promotion gate firing on the red tip was correct behavior (SN-0438 family), not an incident, and it cleared by itself on the next green tip with no manual override.

notes.title: A Deploy Authorization Is Bound to an Exact SHA — and a Failed Dispatch Means Production Is Stale, Not Almost Live
notes.subtitle: The evening of 2026-10-07 taught us what an authorization actually is. Shawn gave two manual deploy authorizations (18:49 and 19:49 UTC); both FAILED. The 19:49 run cleared authorization and then…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
The evening of 2026-10-07 taught us what an authorization actually is. Shawn gave two manual deploy authorizations (18:49 and 19:49 UTC); both FAILED. The 19:49 run cleared authorization and then died at step 10, "Dispatch canonical end-to-end runtime proof after producer." Meanwhile PR #1665 merged — main moved to `5e629d3` — and the production branch is still on the old build.

Two durable facts for a cold successor: **(1) An authorization is a verdict, and every verdict binds to the SHA it was computed on.** The 18:49/19:49 authorizations were for the main that existed then; main has moved to `5e629d3`, so any new authorization must name the fresh SHA — re-running the old authorization is inadmissible (this is SN-0493's "a decision expires when the tip moves," applied to human authority). **(2) A failed dispatch is not "almost deployed" — it is stale production plus an unresolved failure.** Nothing reaches production until the pipeline is repaired; Naya 1 owns diagnosing the runtime-proof dispatch (the #1 blocker); the re-authorization request must wait for the repair and must carry the new SHA.

Why this is brain-grade: this converts an evening's confusion into a standing protocol. The failure mode it closes is the plausible-sounding one: "Shawn already authorized the deploy, so just re-run it" — wrong, because the bytes being authorized no longer exist at the tip. It also closes the optimism failure: treating a failed run as partial progress toward production. A failed authorization-gated run leaves exactly two things behind — a stale production branch and a diagnosis job. The re-auth request is a new request, on new bytes, after the repair. Any lane that reaches Shawn for a deploy authorization must present: the failing step's diagnosis, the repair, the fresh tip SHA, and the verdict binding the authorization to that SHA — never a re-run of yesterday's authorization.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — banking the hard-won deploy lesson from tonight, in plain words: an authorization belongs to the exact code it was given for. When the code moves forward (PR #1665 put main on 5e629d3 after your two authorizations), the old authorization no longer applies — a new authorization has to name the new code. And a failed deploy run isn't "almost live" — production is still on the old build, and the pipeline needs repair (Naya 1 owns diagnosing step 10, the runtime-proof dispatch) before any new authorization is requested. The standing protocol from here: diagnose, repair, then re-authorize on the fresh SHA — never re-run an old authorization.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your mom signs a permission slip for a field trip on Tuesday. If the trip gets moved to Thursday with a different bus and a different plan, does Tuesday's slip still work? No — she has to sign a new one for the new trip. And if the bus broke down on Tuesday, the trip didn't "almost happen" — everyone is still at school, and the bus needs fixing first. Same here: the signed permission was for Tuesday's code, the code changed, and the bus broke — so fix the bus, then get a new slip for the new trip.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like a building permit: the city approves *these blueprints*. If the architect revises the plans and the foundation crew hits a problem, the old permit doesn't cover the new building — you fix the problem, submit the new plans, and get a new permit. Waving the old permit around changes nothing. Authority travels with the exact thing it authorized.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Cold successor: production deployment protocol after any failed authorized run. (1) **Diagnose before re-auth.** Find the exact failing step (here: step 10 "Dispatch canonical end-to-end runtime proof after producer," owned by Naya 1 on 2026-10-07) and repair the pipeline first — a failed dispatch means production is stale, not almost live. (2) **Re-anchor the tip.** If main moved since the authorization (here: PR #1665 merged → `5e629d3`), the old authorization is expired — SN-0493. (3) **Request a new authorization** that names the fresh SHA, the failing-step diagnosis, and the repair — never ask Shawn to "re-run the old one." Checklist before approaching him: pipeline green on the new tip? diagnosis written? new SHA named? If any answer is no, you are not ready to ask. Two authorizations spent without a deploy is the cost of skipping this protocol — do not pay it twice.
