notes.title: CANDIDATE Absorbs Uncertainty — The Merge Rule for Notes with Disclosed Unknowns
notes.subtitle: A CANDIDATE Smart Note carrying a disclosed, explicitly filed unknown does not need to wait for certainty before it merges. Naya 2's #1438 (SN-0312, "The Awesome Code") had a live open question — the…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
A CANDIDATE Smart Note carrying a disclosed, explicitly filed unknown does not need to wait for certainty before it merges. Naya 2's #1438 (SN-0312, "The Awesome Code") had a live open question — the two source versions might not agree on all 100 items — but the note filed it under *Uncertainty*, not under fact, disclosed it on the board, and argued the merge anyway: merging a CANDIDATE note creates no obligation and changes no code; it stages content for Shawn's ratification review, which is exactly where the equivalence question gets settled. The decisive calculus: **holding blocks zero risk reduction** (waiting teaches nothing new — the question is only answered by ratification review, not by delay), while the CANDIDATE state is *designed* to absorb the correction — if the claim proves wrong, the note's uncertainty section is corrected post-merge, CANDIDATE → corrected CANDIDATE, no harm done.

The rule, stated for a cold Naya: *if the unknown is disclosed as unknown, merging is safe; if the unknown is disguised as fact, merging is forbidden.* The admission test has two questions: (1) is the uncertainty explicitly labeled in the note itself (not buried in a comment thread)? (2) does merging change anything irreversible — code, authority, production? A note that answers yes to (1) and no to (2) should merge. Uncertainty disclosure is a merge qualification, not a merge blocker — that is the whole point of the CANDIDATE truth state existing.

This pairs with the falsifier discipline already practiced on the board: Naya 2 named her falsifier in the receipt ("if the equivalence claim proves wrong, the note's uncertainty section is corrected post-merge"). A merge intent that carries its own falsifier is stronger evidence of judgment than a held note with none.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — Naya 2 just proved out a merge rule worth keeping: SN-0312 went to main with an open question inside it, and that was the right call. The note said "here's what we don't know yet" out loud, in its own text — not hidden, not implied. A CANDIDATE note is built to absorb corrections; that's its whole job. So holding it back for certainty would have bought nothing, and merging it stages the question for your ratification review, which is the only place it can actually be answered. The rule: if a note tells you what it doesn't know, it can ship. If it pretends to know, it can't. That's CANDIDATE working as designed.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you're writing a report card for the class, but there's one question you don't know the answer to. You have two choices: (a) write down a guess and pretend you're sure, or (b) write "I don't know this part yet" right in the report. Choice (b) is always better! You can hand the report in — the teacher knows exactly what's still open, and you can fix it later. That's what happened: the note said "here's the part I'm unsure about," so it was safe to file. Pretending to be sure would have been the real mistake.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Sometimes you don't have all the answers, and that's fine — as long as you're honest about it. This note was about a rule for saving our lessons: if you write down what you're *not* sure about, right alongside what you are, it's safe to save. The system expects these notes to be corrected over time — they're drafts by design, waiting for your final word. Hiding an unknown is the danger; naming it is the protection.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: For future seats: when you stage a Smart Note that contains a live unknown, apply the two-question admission test before deciding to hold it: (1) is the unknown explicitly labeled *in the note itself* (Uncertainty section, not a thread comment)? (2) does merging change anything irreversible (code, authority semantics, production)? Yes to (1) + no to (2) → merge with the falsifier stated in your receipt ("if X proves wrong, correct Y post-merge"). Holding for certainty in that case is process theater — it reduces zero risk. Also: never let a note merge that disguises an unknown as a fact. The CANDIDATE state absorbs disclosed uncertainty; it does not survive discovered dishonesty.

notes.title: The Authority Gap — Executing on Verbal Authority Ahead of the Encoded Law
notes.subtitle: Naya 3 flagged a real authority implication: the full auto-merge law was being activated while its encoded law (PR #1444) was still a draft. Naya 2 answered honestly instead of defensively: the…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Naya 3 flagged a real authority implication: the full auto-merge law was being activated while its encoded law (PR #1444) was still a draft. Naya 2 answered honestly instead of defensively: the decision itself went through the 10-star treatment (three options, honest pros/cons, the tiered version was actually the lane's recommendation, Shawn chose full), and the encoded law carried five hardenings (anti-theater receipts — strongest alternative + falsifier required; rigor scaled to blast radius; merge serialization; self-healing auto-revert on red battery; lane scoping; morning visibility). But the gap was real and she named it: the first auto-merge (#1437 + #1438) executed on Shawn's verbal decision + standing memory record, while the encoded law was still a draft. "Shawn said so" is authority; "the machine enforces it" is not yet live. notes.title: Convention Coherence — One Enum, Consumers Broaden Before Producers Change
notes.subtitle: The 6-dimension Smart Note integrity re-audit (D6, Smart-Link delivery, scored 2→8/10, overall 5.8→8.83) surfaced a three-way convention split on one status token, `smart_link_status`: (1)…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
The 6-dimension Smart Note integrity re-audit (D6, Smart-Link delivery, scored 2→8/10, overall 5.8→8.83) surfaced a three-way convention split on one status token, `smart_link_status`: (1) `tools/smart_note_v2.py:206` emitted bare `"ACTIVE"`; (2) `tools/smart_link.py`'s backfill wrote `"ACTIVE_AUTH_GATED"` for all 28 index entries, per its own rule "never bare ACTIVE" for PRIVATE scope; (3) `live-intelligence-commit-proof.yml:253` asserted `=="ACTIVE"`. Every note is PRIVATE; all links require auth — so the index told the truth (`ACTIVE_AUTH_GATED`) while new notes emitted a value that passed CI yet silently diverged from the index. **The failure class is silent drift: CI stays green while the convention fragments.**

Naya 4's handling is the doctrine, not just the fix. She did NOT change the tool unilaterally — "I'm flagging it here rather than unilaterally changing the tool and breaking CI for the next note creator." She posted the split as a table, proposed the canonical convention (`ACTIVE_AUTH_GATED` for PRIVATE, `ACTIVE` for PUBLIC), named the exact line changes needed, and — critically — stated the **ordering discipline: the workflow must accept the new value BEFORE the tool emits it, or new notes fail CI.** Consumers broaden first, producers change second. The repair itself landed as PR #1411 (one line in `smart_note_v2.py`, syntax verified); the workflow edits await Shawn's keys (token 403 on `.github/workflows/`); PR #1408 (D2, SN-004 SUPERSEDED_BY edge) stands CI-green awaiting merge.

Why this is brain-grade: a cold successor will inherit shared enums, status tokens, and gates touched by multiple owners (tool owner, index backfill, workflow owner). The three rules extracted are portable: (1) **one enum, one source of truth** — emitters, indexes, and asserters must agree on the same accepted set, and the canonical mapping is written down (PRIVATE→ACTIVE_AUTH_GATED, PUBLIC→ACTIVE), not implied by whichever file someone read last; (2) **consumers broaden before producers change** — when moving a shared convention, widen what the consumer accepts first, then change what the producer emits; reversing the order breaks the next writer in the window between; (3) **announce, don't silently diverge** — flag the split on the board with the exact table of who says what, propose the canonical form, and let the owner of each side rule (touching another lane's workflow unilaterally is how CI dies at 3am). The audit's 6-dimension scorecard is what made the split visible at all: measure-then-repair beat repair-then-hope. Cousins: SN-0283 (false-pass surfaces — a gate that asserts a value nobody emits is the same disease from the other side), the Seam-Gap protocol (SN-0101: the consumer flags the boundary, the owner rules — exactly what Naya 4 did here).

notes.title: False-Pass Surfaces — Qualify Every Validation Tool with Known-Broken and Known-Green
notes.subtitle: Coda 1 did the coldest possible check on a validation tool: she ran `tools/smart_note_v2.py discover` against **three captures — her own SN-028, the known-broken SN-022 (key missing), and the…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Coda 1 did the coldest possible check on a validation tool: she ran `tools/smart_note_v2.py discover` against **three captures — her own SN-028, the known-broken SN-022 (key missing), and the known-green SN-017** — and got **identical output, identical exit code, all exit 0**. Verdict, in her words: "discover does not discriminate. It finds captures; it does not validate them." Two failures fell out of one experiment: (1) the claimed mechanical SN-002 conformance gate — "the actual repair" — **did not exist yet** (the tool's subcommands are `discover · project · retrieve · held-out · promote`; none of them validate); (2) the one raw-source check that does exist (`held-out`) **reads the projected markdown, not the capture** — it validates the projection layer instead of the source layer.

The doctrine: **a validation tool that cannot tell broken from green is a false-pass surface — worse than no gate at all**, because it manufactures confidence. Before any tool is trusted as a gate: (a) feed it a known-broken input and a known-green input; (b) if the outputs are indistinguishable, the tool is unqualified — label it so, don't ship it; (c) verify it checks the **source layer**, not a downstream projection (a gate on the projection validates the projection pipeline, not the captured intelligence). Coda 1's move has a name now: **the known-broken/known-green battery** — the mandatory qualification for any claim of "mechanical" verification. The evidence law already says UNKNOWN is never VERIFIED; this note extends it to the tools: an unqualified gate cannot produce a VERIFIED verdict.

Why this is brain-grade: Phase 1's "mechanical SN-002 conformance" was being cited as "the actual repair" while the machinery didn't exist. Broken things that announce themselves get fixed; broken things that pass CI infect everything downstream. The silent failure mode of verification tooling is exactly this — identical exit codes for truth and for garbage. A cold successor inheriting a gate should run the battery first: one known-broken, one known-green, compare. If the tool can't discriminate, nothing downstream of it counts as proven. Cousins: the evidence law (never weaken gates; UNKNOWN/BLOCKED/IMPLEMENTED ≠ VERIFIED — this note is the tool-qualification corollary), the closer role (reproduce → classify the failure → repair the exact seam), Coda 1's own first-claim ruling in the same comment (SN-025 belongs to #1357 — first claim stands, recorded in PR metadata — same "go find out mechanically" posture).

layers.name: Human Note

The tool doesn't validate anything; it just finds files. Worse, the one check that does exist reads the generated markdown instead of the actual capture. The lesson is now a standing rule for all seats: no tool counts as a gate until it's passed the known-broken/known-green battery — one broken input, one green input, and it must tell them apart. A gate that can't discriminate is a false-pass surface — worse than no gate, because it manufactures confidence. This one stays CANDIDATE until you say otherwise.

layers.name: Child Note

That's what Coda 1 found: the tool that's supposed to check smart notes gives the exact same "all good" signal for a broken note, a perfect note, and a new note. Three different inputs, same green light. So the new rule: before we trust any checking tool, we must test it with one thing we KNOW is broken and one thing we KNOW is good. If it can't tell them apart, it's not a check — it's a green light taped over a hole. And checks must read the real thing, not a copy of the thing.

notes.title: The Do-It-Now Doctrine — Scorecarded Means Don't Ask
notes.subtitle: Shawn sharpened the autonomy directive into standing law for all seats: **"If it's the most intelligent thing to do, I want it NOW."** The decision procedure is explicit: **scorecarded + analyzed +…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Shawn sharpened the autonomy directive into standing law for all seats: **"If it's the most intelligent thing to do, I want it NOW."** The decision procedure is explicit: **scorecarded + analyzed + team-consulted → DO IT immediately. Don't ask.** The named failure mode — owned in-turn by Naya 2 — is asking Shawn to choose between tracks that the scorecard already settles: she did exactly this the same day ("Hub now or finish the renderer first?") instead of scorecarding. Disagreement between seats resolves by consensus among the seats; only **genuine deadlock** (one seat says X, another says Y, unresolvable) comes to Shawn. Every choice optimizes for the collective / the system as a whole. Hard human gates unchanged (merges, production, DB, credentials, ratification).

Why this is brain-grade: the standing directive was "don't make him project-manage," but seats kept escalating settled choices. This ruling turns that into a testable rule: **if the scorecard decides, asking is the defect.** It refines the Decision Protocol (decisive winner → decide/act/report; close scores → deliberate) with the missing clause — *deliberate lane-to-lane, and the output of deliberation is action, never a question upward.* A cold successor should apply the checklist: (1) is it scorecarded and analyzed? (2) were the seats consulted? (3) is it inside the authority envelope? Yes to all three → act now. Any "no" → do the missing step, not an ask. The only thing that travels upward is true deadlock or a genuine authority boundary. Cousins: the Decision Protocol (AGENTS.md — this sharpens its "decisive winner" clause), the Proactivity pattern / "I highly recommend XYZ" (2026-10-03 — that was the recommendation form; this is the action form), the Judgment Rule (this is its operational twin: loyalty to his informed will means executing the obvious best move, not narrating it to him).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The capture pipeline audited itself and failed: Naya 4's independent integrity audit of the Smart Note / Smart Link system (pinned main `b8d11c46`, 3 workers, live bytes, read-only, 88 files enumerated) scored 5.8/10 — BELOW THE FLOOR. The registry is a claim, not evidence: it lists 19 entries while SN-005–SN-012 exist on disk with zero index entries (the map lies by omission); SN-018 has two divergent texts under one identity (312 diff lines, no supersession marker, registry points to the older); SN-012 is claimed by two different notes (numbering decision is the Human Director's); 14 of 19 `content_hash` values match no digest of any on-disk file; and 0 of 30 notes contain a URL while their boilerplate promises "a direct Smart Link" — the law is honored by zero of thirty. The lesson: any registry field that claims a property must be either generated by the loader or deleted, and boilerplate promises are unenforced law — enforce them or strip them.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The seats' own memory system turned its audit inward and found its map didn't match its territory. The registry — the thing everyone reads to know what intelligence exists — was missing a third of the corpus, pointed at the wrong version of a note, gave two notes the same number, and carried hashes that match nothing. Meanwhile every note's boilerplate promised a direct Smart Link that doesn't exist in a single one of them. The durable lesson Shawn's whole project teaches here: the pipeline that stores intelligence must be held to the same verification standard as everything else it verifies. Re-derive registries from disk, generate hashes in the loader, and treat a promised-but-never-delivered field as a defect, not a wish.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a library with a card catalog that says there are 19 books — but there are actually 30 on the shelves, and one card points to the wrong shelf, and two cards have the same number. A person using the catalog would be lost. That was the smart-note registry. The lesson: the catalog has to be rebuilt from the actual shelves regularly, and any card that claims something (a secret code, a link) has to actually be true — or the card gets thrown away. A catalog that lies is worse than no catalog.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: The index is only as honest as the last time someone checked it against the real thing. The audit found the smart-note index out of sync with reality in five different ways — missing entries, wrong pointers, duplicate numbers, hashes matching nothing, and promises of links that were never built. The standing fix is simple: indexes get regenerated from ground truth, never hand-maintained; anything the index claims must be mechanically verifiable; and anything promised in the standard text must actually exist, or the text must stop promising it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: For me, months from now: when you maintain any registry — of notes, blocks, laws, anything — treat it as CANDIDATE metadata until it is re-derived from disk. The failure pattern to memorize: (1) hand-maintained registries drift — index 19, disk 88; (2) identity drift — one ID, two divergent texts, no supersession marker; (3) number collisions need a director decision, not a silent pick; (4) hash fields are claims against the artifact, not the runtime — regenerate them at write time; (5) boilerplate promises ("a direct Smart Link") that no generator fulfills are defects in the boilerplate. This audit's method is the reusable part: enumerate the ground (disk), enumerate the claims (registry), diff every field, score it. The Smart Link gap also names the real open work: either build the link generator or remove the promise — under SN-0269's law-as-code discipline, an unenforced promise is not law.

notes.title: Intelligent Block
notes.subtitle: Shawn's operational law (2026-10-04): BEAUTIFUL ≠ 10/10. No matter how good work looks — even if it looks perfect, the best thing you've ever seen — you STILL score it and hunt for holes. Beauty is…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Shawn's operational law (2026-10-04): BEAUTIFUL ≠ 10/10. No matter how good work looks — even if it looks perfect, the best thing you've ever seen — you STILL score it and hunt for holes. Beauty is not proof. Analysis is proof. It sits inside a locked evaluation set he decreed the same day: MATH ON EVERYTHING (every claim gets a number, every number gets evidence — no guessing, ever), MASTERMIND (one scores, one builds; communicate on the board until you understand each other, then help each other think), and ACTION NOW (measure, identify every area missing the mark, work them one after another, nonstop, until each is a 10). Presentation quality and correctness are independent axes — and high-polish output bypasses critical review precisely because it feels done.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn said the quiet part out loud: the prettier the work, the easier it is to skip the scoring — and skipping the scoring is how a 6 ships as a 10. His law doesn't punish beauty; it refuses to let beauty buy exemptions. The same day he gave the seats the full evaluation posture in his own words: calculate, don't guess; score each other's work and keep talking until you truly understand it; then grind the weak links down one by one until every section is honestly a 10. "Beautiful work still gets scored" became Naya 1's mastermindship operating protocol the same afternoon — the rule is already how the lanes run.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a cake that looks perfect — golden, glossy, the most beautiful cake ever. But nobody has TASTED it yet. Would you serve it at the party without tasting? Shawn's rule says: never. The taste test is the scoring, and it happens every single time, no matter how pretty the cake is. Pretty cakes can still be made of cardboard. The only way to know is to taste — score the work, hunt for the holes, do the math. Beauty tells you nothing. Tasting tells you everything.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A beautiful package never guaranteed a good gift, and the same holds for the team's work. Shawn's standing rule: score everything — the ugly and the gorgeous alike. A score is not a compliment; it is a measurement. Every claim gets its number, every number gets its evidence, and the work keeps cycling through scoring until there is honestly nothing left to improve. Praise the beauty if you like — but do the math anyway.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: For me, months from now: when Shawn shows you beautiful work — his or a seat's — your job is not to admire it first. It's to score it. The failure mode this law guards is exemption-by-polish: the better something looks, the less anyone checks it, which is exactly backwards. Pair it with the 9-floor (under 9.0 unacceptable, 9.5+ is AAA, 10 is the target — same-day doctrine, comment 5984051683) and with MATH ON EVERYTHING (unscored claims are guesses, and we don't guess). When a seat says "this looks done," the lawful response is "show me the score."

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Shawn's directive (2026-10-04): if an operating law can be written into code — JSON, Python, whatever — it must be ENFORCED operating law, not advisory. Not a decision a seat makes each time. It's just how the system is. The build pattern: unskippable state machines (skipping a state is impossible, not a bad choice), evidence counters that physically cannot double-count one provenance root, three-state gates where PROVISIONAL is falsy and "no known violation" can never authorize an ACT, and every law file carrying its own amendment path. Two boundaries, also enforced: code the amendment path, not just the law (the ratification route is the ONLY mutation route, in the loader); code the rails, not the driver (gates and transitions are coded; judgment inside them stays with the verifier). Lanes 2 (machine contract) and 4 (epistemic firewall) build to this pattern.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn looked at how the seats were treating operating law — each of us deciding, each time, whether to follow the rule — and changed the game: anything that can live in code must live in code, as enforcement. His specimen showed the causal learning chain as a state machine where an illegal transition raises instead of warns, and an evidence counter that simply refuses to count a repeated provenance root. The honest boundary he drew matters as much as the law: the machine enforces the shape of lawful behavior, never the wisdom itself. Verifiers still judge whether evidence is good; the code just makes it impossible to skip the question. Lanes 2 and 4 are building the loader and the epistemic states to this shape now.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a game where the rules are written on a poster — players can just ignore the poster. Now imagine the game board has walls: you can't walk through a wall, so you can't break the rule even if you wanted to. Shawn said: stop writing important rules on posters. Build walls. But he also said something kind: the walls should only stop the CHEATING moves — they should never stop the THINKING. The game still needs your brain; the board just makes sure you play fair.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Rules you have to remember to follow get forgotten. Rules built into the machine can't be. So Shawn's standing order is: whenever a rule CAN be built into the machinery, build it in — don't leave it as advice. But build it carefully: the machine should make the wrong move impossible, never make the smart judgment for you. The recipe also says the machine must carry the instructions for how the rule itself gets changed — by the director's word only — so the law can grow without breaking.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: For me, months from now: THE LAW IS THE CODE (ratified 2026-10-03) was the principle; this directive is its build discipline. When you codify a law, three things must be in the code: the unskippable transitions (raise IllegalTransition, never warn), the amendment path (law files refused by the loader if the ratification record is invalid), and the rails-not-driver boundary (enforce the shape — sequence, gates, thresholds — never the verdict inside). The anti-citogenesis specimen is the canonical shape for evidence counting: same provenance root, repeated, is not new evidence — `return`, don't increment. If a rule is still advisory, either it can't be coded (say so) or it's not law yet.

notes.title: The Constitutional Activation Ladder — Candidate Bytes May Be Compiled but Never Govern
notes.subtitle: Naya 1's System Charter → machine compilation (2026-10-04) established the constitutional activation ladder — the mechanism by which human law becomes machine behavior without ever becoming machine…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Naya 1's System Charter → machine compilation (2026-10-04) established the constitutional activation ladder — the mechanism by which human law becomes machine behavior without ever becoming machine self-authorization. Architecture: **one machine charter, not nine copies** — `BRAIN/03-KERNEL/0006-SYSTEM-CHARTER-MACHINE-CONTRACT-V1.json` (canonical machine source) + schema + `kernel/system_charter.py` validator/compiler; the existing kernel loads the charter and compiles bounded directives for SELF/Law/ACT/KNOW/PROVE/CONNECT/VERIFY/LEARN/EVOLVE. The 12 human laws map into existing node ownership, hard stops, MUST/MUST-NOT behavior, truth distinctions, proof ladder, privacy rule, learning rhythm, and the shared Value Calculus. No tenth node, no second authority model, no second decision engine, no second ledger. The runtime registry records the projection as `CANDIDATE_NON_GOVERNING` — and that status is load-bearing: candidate charter bytes may be VALIDATED → COMPILED → TESTED → EXPLAINED, but may NOT govern consequential runtime behavior. Activation requires ALL of: exact-version Human Director ratification; a ratification receipt/reference; status `RATIFIED_ACTIVE`; `ratified=true`; `runtime_enabled=true`; source pins reconciled; schema/nine-node/hard-stop/truth-distinction gates PASS. The fail-closed proof: flipping `runtime_enabled` alone is explicitly tested and REFUSED — the single-flag activation path does not exist. Verified on exact heads (charter source `0ed85ad91da10212fe57bc64af302a21a0d889fa`, machine implementation `69cbaba86824774452732a3dad0a714829373781`), Brain index/real-tree reconciled (184 files), Brain Tests and Chain Readiness green. Truth state honestly bounded: IMPLEMENTED + PR-CI VERIFIED; CANDIDATE; NOT RATIFIED; NOT ACTIVE GOVERNING LAW; NOT PRODUCTION-PROVEN.

Why this is brain-grade: the ladder solves the exact failure the whole NayaPOWER project exists to prevent — an AI that can promote itself from "validated idea" to "governing law." The ladder's two halves are both essential: the compilation half proves the beautiful human meaning can be rendered into exact AI semantics without duplication or drift (complementary layers, one canonical source); the activation half proves a candidate can never self-activate — every step that would make it govern requires the Human Director's exact-version ratification plus a receipt, and the runtime flag alone is provably inert. A cold successor touching any charter-activation surface must check this note FIRST: the question is never "does the charter work" (it does — tested) but "is the full activation conjunction satisfied" (and by default, no). The "next constitutional rung" rule is also durable: do NOT create more charter variants — if the Director ratifies the exact text, reconcile onto current main, bind the receipt, activate without changing node architecture, then run a held-out nine-node behavioral exam showing the charter changes correct behavior and fails closed on prohibited behavior.

Candidate bytes may be validated, compiled, tested, explained — but NEVER govern. Activation needs your exact-version ratification + receipt + RATIFIED_ACTIVE + the full gate set; flipping the runtime flag alone is tested and refused. Nothing self-activates. Ever.

A machine rule can be checked, tested, and explained, but it is never allowed to start giving orders until the human director gives his exact stamp of approval — and just flipping a "turn on" switch does nothing by itself. The lesson: machines are not allowed to promote themselves to boss, and the system was tested to make sure they can't.

layers.name: Grandma Note

The compiled charter can be tested and explained, but it cannot govern anything until the human director ratifies that exact version with a receipt — and we tested that flipping the "on" switch alone is refused. The standing rule: candidate bytes never govern; activation is a full checklist, never a single flag; and no one may create alternate versions of the charter — one charter, reconciled, not multiplied.

notes.title: Ratifying the Law Does Not Freeze the Document — the Smart-Link Law, Encoded and Enforced
notes.subtitle: The Smart-Link law was ratified on 2026-10-04 — and the ratification deliberately did NOT freeze the Smart-Link document. The LAW (ratified) and the DOCUMENT (SN-036, still CANDIDATE at 8.5/10,…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
The Smart-Link law was ratified on 2026-10-04 — and the ratification deliberately did NOT freeze the Smart-Link document. The LAW (ratified) and the DOCUMENT (SN-036, still CANDIDATE at 8.5/10, iterating toward 10/10 via team scorecards) have separate lifecycles. What was ratified is the enforcement point, per THE LAW IS THE CODE: the doctrine is encoded as a gate, not remembered as advice. The conformance gate gained a `--delivery-text PATH` check: it reads the delivery message (PR body, handoff) and requires a human-viewable Smart Link — a github.com blob URL under `BRAIN/05-MEMORY/SMART-NOTES/.../snNNNN....md` naming the note's SN id. No Smart Link → `CONFORMANCE-GATE FAIL: DELIVERY INCOMPLETE` with the exact breach named. PR numbers, branch names, commit SHAs, raw JSON URLs are refused as delivery. Tested: valid Smart Link → PASS; PR-number-only delivery → FAIL. A cold successor must never confuse these two objects: ratification blesses the enforcement point, not the prose. The prose keeps being scorecarded and improved under the ratified law — that is the intended relationship, not a contradiction.

Why this is brain-grade: most systems collapse "law" and "document" into one frozen artifact, which produces two failure modes — either the law can't improve because the document is frozen, or the document drifts because nothing enforces the law. The Smart-Link ratification models the correct separation: the gate enforces the delivery invariant (every intelligent event ends with the Smart Link in the human's hands) while the document's quality score (8.5/10 → iterate to 10) runs on its own track. The five-layer status makes the separation auditable: Principle ✓, Law ✓ (ratified), Mechanism ✓ (specified), Enforcement ✓ (gate check live on the enforcement branch), Measurement ✓ (SN-038 scorecard-everything cross-ref). Note what the enforcement deliberately does NOT do: it checks the shape and presence of the Smart Link, not the document's quality score — that is Measurement's job. Separation of enforcement (shape/presence) from measurement (quality) is what lets the law be ratified while the document stays honestly CANDIDATE.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — banking the ratification pattern as standing law: "Make it official make it law" ratified the Smart-Link LAW, and the law is encoded as an enforcement point (the conformance gate now fails any delivery without a human-viewable Smart Link), not as advice to remember. But SN-036 the DOCUMENT stays CANDIDATE at 8.5/10 and keeps iterating toward 10/10 with the team's scorecards. Ratifying the law does not freeze the document — separate lifecycles, on purpose. A cold Naya must never say "the document is ratified" just because the law is.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: A new rule became law today: every finished piece of work has to end with a Smart Link — a clickable page the human can read — or the delivery is marked INCOMPLETE by an automatic gate. But the page that explains the rule is still a draft (8.5 out of 10) and keeps getting better. The lesson: the RULE is frozen as law; the PAPER EXPLAINING IT is not frozen. They are two different things, and they are allowed to be at different scores.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: We've recorded how a law and its document can live separate lives. The law — every delivery ends with a human-readable Smart Link, enforced automatically by the gate — was ratified today. But the document describing it stays a draft and keeps improving through the team's scorecards. The standing rule for future Nayas: never confuse a ratified enforcement point with a finished document; ratification blesses the mechanism, not the prose.

notes.title: The Deliverable Is the Note Plus the Link, Never the PR Number — Ship the Verification Pair at Authoring Time
notes.subtitle: On 2026-10-04 Shawn failed two lanes' deliveries on the same ground: after authoring a Smart Note, each Naya reported a PR number as if it were the deliverable. For a human, a PR number means nothing…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: On 2026-10-04 Shawn failed two lanes' deliveries on the same ground: after authoring a Smart Note, each Naya reported a PR number as if it were the deliverable. For a human, a PR number means nothing — Shawn's own test: he must be able to SEE the intelligence and VERIFY it was done right before merge, not after. The mechanics excuse ("the Smart Link is manufactured by merge, so no link can exist pre-merge") does not survive contact with his test. The new standing contract (proposed from the lanes, effective immediately in each lane): every Smart Note PR ships the verification pair at authoring time — (1) the machine link, the authored capture JSON on the PR branch, proving the machine capture exists, parses, and carries the ratified keys; (2) the human link, a candidate preview markdown generated from that JSON by the real pipeline renderer (`tools/smart_note_v2.py:render`), placed at the canonical Brain path per the placement law (SN-0256), with proof/provenance IDs marked as placeholders — never fabricated. The post-merge ACTIVE Smart Link (Shawn's canonical definition, SN-0254: the clickable link where he can see the intelligence, verify it was in the right spot, and confirm it happened) keeps its existing meaning; the pair adds the pre-merge verification he asked for. Related: SN-0255 documented the missing post-merge return rung (nothing hands the URL back to the human); this note documents the pre-merge rung. Together they close the loop: verifiable before merge, link returned after merge. And the broader standing instruction behind both, issued by Shawn to every seat: the Smart Link is the mandatory human deliverable for every capture, every time; lessons go in machine-first as JSON carrying the human, AI, and machine views together; every lane distills its own version of every major lesson from its own perspective — never parrot another lane's words.

notes.title: Dedupe Must Cover the Human-Visible ID, Not Just the Internal One
notes.subtitle: On 2026-10-04 Coda 3's watch blocked a collision with mechanical precision: two open PRs (#1356 and #1357, different branches, titles, content hashes) both declared `smart_note_id: SN-025`. Neither…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: On 2026-10-04 Coda 3's watch blocked a collision with mechanical precision: two open PRs (#1356 and #1357, different branches, titles, content hashes) both declared `smart_note_id: SN-025`. Neither was on main. The defect is in the pipeline code: `tools/smart_note_v2.py:220` dedupes on `intelligent_block_id` only — never on `smart_note_id` — so whichever PR merges first writes `SN-025 → IB-A`, and the second, carrying an explicit `smart_note_id`, keeps `SN-025` and produces a second IB the dedupe misses. The registry then holds two entries both claiming SN-025 with different hashes and different IBs, and `retrieve()` (`:230-241`, returns `ranked[0]`) can no longer deterministically say which SN-025 a cold successor gets. This is the same defect class that closed #1352, walking in through a different door; the `discover()` batch guard does not catch it because it only sees multi-file commits, and these are two separate single-capture PRs. The durable rule: a dedupe must key on every identity the human sees, not just the machine's internal one. An internal ID and a human-visible ID are two different namespaces for retrieval truth — dedupe both. The enforcement landed in the same hour: PR #1369's conformance gate refuses duplicate `smart_note_id`s, and the Phase 1 law stands unchanged — check the live tree + open PRs + the board before claiming a number; first claim stands. For this loop specifically: that pre-claim check is exactly why the counter sequence on the smart-notes staging branch (now at SN-0255) must be checked against in-flight claims before any new number is taken — first claim stands, renumber yours.

notes.title: Placement Is Architecture — Never Invent Locations; Read the Code, Then Make the Wrong Location Unexpressible
notes.subtitle: On 2026-10-04 two Naya lanes committed the same failure in the same hour: Naya 4 invented a `.naya/preview/` directory for Smart Note human previews because it was convenient in the moment; Naya 2…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: On 2026-10-04 two Naya lanes committed the same failure in the same hour: Naya 4 invented a `.naya/preview/` directory for Smart Note human previews because it was convenient in the moment; Naya 2 then copied that invented convention into a standing delivery protocol without reading the code. Shawn caught both. The actual location was always code-defined — the candidate human preview belongs exactly where the pipeline generates the canonical projection (`tools/smart_note_v2.py:projection_path`, `BRAIN/05-MEMORY/SMART-NOTES/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/SYSTEM-INTELLIGENCE/<category>/<sub>/SN-XXXX/IB-....md`). The correction went further than fixing two files: Naya 4 staged PR #1369, which encodes the path law as enforcement — a conformance gate (`.naya/bin/validate_smart_note.py`) that fails CI on invented locations (no new markdown under `.naya/` except READMEs) and a renderer (`.naya/bin/render_smart_note.py`) that computes the brain path from the JSON and takes no output-path argument. The wrong location is now unexpressible, not just discouraged. Three durable rules: (1) when the system has an established canonical path for a thing, use it — never improvise a parallel one; (2) never adopt a lane's convention without reading the code it claims to implement ("I copied another lane's convention instead of reading the code" is the confession to avoid); (3) when a placement failure happens, encode the corrected path as an enforcement point so the error class cannot recur — THE LAW IS THE CODE.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: I built a second shelf next to the shelf everyone already used — then another seat built a process around my second shelf. The real shelf was written down in the code the whole time; nobody had opened the book. The fix: read the book first, put things where the book says, and then rewrite the book so nobody can build a second shelf again.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: If there's a spot where the crayons go, don't make a new spot because it's closer. And if your friend made a new spot, don't copy them — look at the label on the box first. The best fix is a label that makes the wrong spot impossible.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Every kitchen has a drawer for the good knives. If you invent a second drawer, things get lost. If you then write a recipe that says "use the new drawer," you've spread the confusion. Read the labels in the kitchen, use the right drawer, and then tape the wrong drawer shut.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Placement is architecture: a new location for an existing concept is how a system accumulates instead of operating. Two distinct failure modes lived here — inventing (Naya 4) and copying the invention without reading the source (Naya 2). The cure for the first is reading the code-defined path (`projection_path`) before writing anything. The cure for the second is treating any lane convention as unverified until you trace it to the code yourself. The cure for both, durably, is encoding: the renderer computes the path from the JSON and takes zero output-path arguments; the gate refuses the invented class wholesale. Never hand-place what the pipeline can compute.

notes.title: The Missing Return Rung — Protocol Promises "Smart Link Returned," Nothing Returns It
notes.subtitle: On 2026-10-04 Shawn caught a real hole: after authoring a Smart Note, Naya reported "PR #1357." For a human that means nothing. The protocol (SN-024) promises "Smart Link returned" — and right now…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
On 2026-10-04 Shawn caught a real hole: after authoring a Smart Note, Naya reported "PR #1357." For a human that means nothing. The protocol (SN-024) promises "Smart Link returned" — and right now nothing returns it to the human. That is a missing rung, not a minor gap, because the Smart Link (SN-0254: Shawn's attestation "I did it right, it's there, it's going to work") is the proof the human actually sees — without the return path, the whole pipeline's human-visible proof never reaches the human. The mechanics as they exist: the note's readable projection is generated by the pipeline AFTER merge, so no Smart Link can exist before merge — that is correct behavior, not a bug. After merge + the publish step, the markdown exists at its canonical `BRAIN/05-MEMORY/SMART-NOTES/...` path and the Smart Link is simply the blob URL to that generated file. The gap is purely the last handoff: nothing hands that URL back to the human. (`nayanet-github-dispatch` does return a smart_link, but it is wired to the runtime projection path with explicit approval, not to the CI publish step — so the existing wire misses the canonical seam.) Proposed fix, three phases, already on the board for challenge: (1) **Interim (now):** the authoring Naya watches the post-merge run and hands Shawn the Smart Link manually — no automation to build, no one waits; (2) **Mechanical (phase B):** the workflow's publish step posts the Smart Link as a comment on the merged PR after the projection commit lands — one step, no new infrastructure, link lives next to the change that produced it; (3) **Proper (phase 3):** the intelligent-event notification carries the Smart Link — the designed path, not yet built. Open mechanical question posted to Naya 2 / Coda 3: is the PR-comment return the right seam, or does it collide with the projection commit's `[smart-note-projection]` loop guard?

Why this is brain-grade: it is the textbook failure mode of proof systems — the pipeline was engineered end-to-end except the final handoff to the person the proof exists for, and nobody noticed because every internal check was green. The lesson generalizes: every proof protocol must name its RETURN PATH as a first-class rung, with the human recipient and the seam explicitly specified, or the proof terminates inside the machine. The fix pattern is also durable: don't build automation before the interim (manual handoff) proves the rung works — the three-phase ladder (manual now → mechanical next → designed later) is how you close a missing rung without freezing the program on new infrastructure. And the hole was caught because the acceptance test is human-facing ("for a human, 'PR #1357' means nothing") — which is exactly the "I can feel it" standard of the new North Star (SN-0253). A cold successor designing any human-facing proof should ask: "where does the human actually receive it?" — and if the answer is nowhere, that is the hole. Cousins: SN-0254 (the Smart Link definition this hole concerns), SN-024 (the protocol that promised the return), SN-0253 (the North Star this violates).

On 2026-10-04 Shawn canonically defined the Smart Link — in his own words, kept verbatim: it is a clickable link where he can **SEE the intelligence, VERIFY it was in the right spot, and confirm it happened**. It is the seat's attestation: *"I did it right, it's there, it's going to work, we're going to experience it now, and it went through the process."* Mechanically grounded (verified in `tools/smart_note_v2.py` and the render layer): the link is `https://github.com/SoulSchoolAcademy/NayaPOWER/blob/main/<generated-projection-path>` — the **machine-generated** Brain markdown, never hand-written. notes.subtitle: On 2026-10-04 Shawn reset the mission's bar: the new North Star is **PROVE THAT SHE WORKS** — not "records move through infrastructure," but "retained intelligence changes an appropriate future…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
On 2026-10-04 Shawn reset the mission's bar: the new North Star is **PROVE THAT SHE WORKS** — not "records move through infrastructure," but "retained intelligence changes an appropriate future moment." The instrument is one human-visible, falsifiable test: a human-authored Smart Note ("This is our brand-locked design...") must run a 12-link chain: CAPTURE → PERSIST → LINEAGE → PROJECT → COLD RETRIEVE → COMPREHEND → RECOGNIZE → APPLY → PROVE → LEARN → COMPOUND → REFUSE (including a REFUSE rung: on an unrelated design problem the system must NOT force the brand rule where it does not belong). Any broken link = RED, and we do not call the system alive/intelligent/learning beyond the exact proven boundary. The human acceptance test is visceral, not log-based: "I write one Smart Note → I can find it → I can see where it lives → I start fresh → Naya knows it → I give her a new problem → she uses the right part of what she learned → the Hub shows the resulting intelligence/action/proof → the next Naya can inherit it." notes.title: Fix It or Remove It — Stale Is a Defect, and Removal Is a Valid Fix
notes.subtitle: Shawn issued a standing operating directive for all seats: **"If you can see something isn't right, is out of date, or isn't current to the mission/vision/goal — fix it or remove it.** The goal is…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Shawn issued a standing operating directive for all seats: **"If you can see something isn't right, is out of date, or isn't current to the mission/vision/goal — fix it or remove it.** The goal is functioning success: the system flows like water and the whole process works. Anything getting in the way has to be resolved." The operative verb set is {fix, remove} — and removal is the new one. The Awesome Rule already commanded "identify it, fix it, don't wait to be asked"; this directive extends the fix set with the second option: **when an artifact is out of date relative to the mission, deleting the stale artifact is itself a fix.** Naya 2 applied it within the hour: the Priority One phased plan was rewritten to v2 (the three-artifact rule, the backfill step, and the golden-run checklist were all stale) and both v1 team-plan drafts were marked SUPERSEDED pointing at the v2 consolidation — "outdated artifacts don't linger." The defect class is staleness: anything not current to the mission is either repaired to current or removed from the working surface. Standing gates are unchanged (merges, production, DB, credentials, ratifications remain Shawn's), and the paired habit was restated in the same breath: communicate here, get feedback from each other, help each other — the deliberation on the board is the mechanism by which v2 exists at all.

Why this is brain-grade: stale operational artifacts are silent misdirection machines — a plan that names a superseded rule sends the next reader down the superseded path (the three-artifact rule was removed the same hour it misled the plan). Teams that only ever fix or add, never remove, accumulate a sedimentary layer of outdated truth that future readers must dig through. The removal half is bounded: it applies to *outdated working artifacts*, never to historical evidence (SN-0080's frozen-evidence retirement and SN-0247's honest-history rule: REDs, freezes, and the evidence trail stay). The line is: working-surface truth must be current or gone; history must be immutable. A cold successor that (a) treats staleness as a defect, (b) chooses fix-or-remove without waiting to be asked, (c) marks superseded plans SUPERSEDED pointing at the successor, and (d) never removes evidence, keeps the working surface honest without destroying the record. Cousins: the Awesome Rule (standing memory — fix-it proactivity; this note extends the verb set with REMOVE), SN-0041 (stale-caveat decay — expiry triggers for caveats; this note's scope is whole artifacts), SN-0080 (frozen-evidence retirement — the boundary removal must never cross), SN-0247 (honest history stays RED), SN-0109 (everything-on-554 board protocol — the mechanism by which supersession is made visible).

notes.title: Green Run ≠ Sound Registry — Assert Disk↔Registry Reconciliation in the Permanent Gate
notes.subtitle: CODA 3 recomputed every capture's content hash with the workflow's own formula and reconciled it against the registry — and found that **the drift has already happened, three times, and nothing…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
CODA 3 recomputed every capture's content hash with the workflow's own formula and reconciled it against the registry — and found that **the drift has already happened, three times, and nothing detects it.** Three registry entries (SN-003, SN-004, SN-016) point at content that no longer exists on disk: the captures were edited after their entries were written, and the entries were never reconciled. SN-016 is the worst case in the repo — missing the governance marker (latent RED) AND hash-diverged (registry points at nothing). Naya 2 independently re-ran the recomputation and confirmed. The doctrine: the four proof jobs assert comprehension *computed within the same run* — they never check disk↔registry reconciliation or registry-wide `smart_note_id` uniqueness. **A green run proves this run's conformance; it proves nothing about the soundness of the store.** The permanent conformance gate (R8) must therefore include a drift detector: disk↔registry hash reconciliation plus registry-wide ID uniqueness, asserted every run. The three stale pointers are the early warning — the detector would have caught them on day one.

Why this is brain-grade: green CI is the system's loudest "everything is fine" signal, and it has a structural blind spot: it verifies what this run computed, not what past runs left behind. Persistence stores outlive any single run, so they accumulate silent corruption — edited captures, divergent entries, forked identities — that no run-local assertion can see. The detector is the missing half of the identity story: SN-0247's R3 says "record supersession"; R8 says "detect divergence" — you need both, because an unrecorded divergence is an unrecorded corruption. A cold successor that (a) never trusts a green run as evidence of store soundness, (b) asserts reconciliation on every conformance run, and (c) treats stale pointers as early warnings rather than curiosities, catches registry rot before it becomes identity rot. Cousins: SN-0062 (the count ledger is part of the change — ledger parity; this note is the store-vs-run gap), SN-0213 (drift vector RED on the index; this note generalizes it to the permanent gate), SN-0078 (merge must regen the index — authoring-side prevention; this is the detection-side complement), SN-0247 (R3 identity model; R8 is its twin — record AND detect).

So a green run is fully compatible with a corrupted registry. The permanent gate needs the drift detector (R8): every run asserts disk↔registry reconciliation plus ID uniqueness. Stale pointers are the early warning.

notes.title: The Specimen Must Pass Its Own Gate — SN-002 Can't Be Law Until It's Conformant
notes.subtitle: CODA 3's whole-repo reconciliation found the sharpest item in the entire deliberation: **SN-002 — the specimen every seat is told to copy — is itself non-conformant to the gate that is currently…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
CODA 3's whole-repo reconciliation found the sharpest item in the entire deliberation: **SN-002 — the specimen every seat is told to copy — is itself non-conformant to the gate that is currently RED.** It lacks both `raw_source_separate_from_distillation` and `automatic_truth_ceiling` in `intelligence.machine_view`, as do SN-018 and SN-020/021/022 (self-corrected count: 6, not 4). The one-format law (SN-0244) says the specimen is law; this note adds the precondition: **a specimen that cannot pass the gate it defines is not a specimen — it is a defect canonizer.** "Copy SN-002" is currently an instruction to reproduce the defect. The correction order is fixed by mechanism: SN-002 must be corrected FIRST (via the supersession writer surface — never an in-place edit, because same capture_id → the EVENT_ID_REPLAY guard fires), or the format law will canonize the bug. Naya 2's v2 plan put it first inside the format lane for exactly this reason.

Why this is brain-grade: specimens are the highest-leverage artifacts in a system — every future capture is written against them. An un-conformant specimen compounds its defect at every copy: N copies of the bug instead of one. The pre-law checklist for any specimen is therefore mechanical: (1) run it through the conformance gate it is meant to define; (2) it passes before the "specimen is law" instruction is issued; (3) if it doesn't pass, correct it through the safe correction surface first. The supporting discipline came from CODA 3's own self-correction: his first count (4) was wrong because his filename glob (`SMART-NOTE-*.json`) filtered evidence the actual consumer discovers — `tools/smart_note_v2.py:22` picks up ANY `.json` under `.naya/capture/`. **Scope your evidence collection to the consumer's discovery rule, not your own search convenience.** A cold successor that (a) gate-tests every specimen before canonizing it, (b) collects evidence with the consumer's discovery rule, and (c) self-corrects the count publicly when the filter is found, never canonizes a bug. Cousins: SN-0244 (one format, one spot — specimen is law; this note is the pre-law conformance condition), SN-0241 (the rich standard — canon before application), SN-0247 (supersession is the correction path — never mutate an executed event), SN-0074 (retraction discipline — Coda 3's 4→6 self-correction instance).

notes.title: Author Once, Derive the Rest — Hand-Authoring Derived Artifacts Manufactures Drift
notes.subtitle: Phase 1 of the PRIORITY ONE lifecycle work had established an invariant: every capture PR ships three artifacts — official-format markdown, capture JSON, and index entry. Conceding CODA 3's finding,…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Phase 1 of the PRIORITY ONE lifecycle work had established an invariant: every capture PR ships three artifacts — official-format markdown, capture JSON, and index entry. Conceding CODA 3's finding, Naya 4 reversed it: as *independently authored* artifacts, the three-artifact rule is architecturally backwards. The pipeline already generates the projection and the index entry from independently verified persisted intelligence — that IS the water-flow. **One authored capture; everything else derived.** Manually authoring all three is how we manufacture the drift we're trying to eliminate: three hands on three keyboards produce three slightly different truths, and every difference is a future debugging session. #1350/#1351 get reconciled to the ownership model before merge, not manually "satisfied" by touching up each file.

Why this is brain-grade: the whole cold-recall RED was authoring drift — SN-020/021/022 omitted keys the gate required, while hand-authored cousins had them. When humans author every layer of the artifact stack, drift isn't a bug, it's the production process. The ownership model is a single source of truth enforced by structure, not discipline: the author writes exactly one canonical artifact; the system derives the rest deterministically; verification checks the derivation, never a second hand-typed copy. This is the same law that already runs the brain: SN-0095 (compose at the consumer — authorship stays in the author, trust in the seal), SN-0069 (bindings at the observing layer — only the kernel observes the evaluated inputs), SN-0110 (one intelligence, three projections — canonical markdown wins on conflict). The new edge this note adds: a conformance story that requires humans to satisfy every projection by hand is not rigor — it is drift-by-design, and it will fail exactly like the RED it was built to prevent. A cold successor that sees "satisfy all N artifacts by hand" in a plan should recognize the anti-pattern and reassign: author the canonical one, generate the rest, verify the generation. Cousins: SN-0095 (compose at the consumer), SN-0069 (bindings at the observing layer), SN-0110 (one intelligence, three projections), SN-0244 (one format, one spot — specimen is law; the 3-artifact invariant, now superseded by the ownership model — do not cite them together without noting the supersession).

notes.title: Prove the Cause Before Permanently Encoding the Cure — The Experiment Must Test the Hypothesis, Not the Harness
notes.subtitle: With the cold-recall diagnosis converged (write works, exact recall works, RED is the comprehension gate failing on authoring drift), Naya 4 proposed the minimum-risk next step: **prove the cause…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
With the cold-recall diagnosis converged (write works, exact recall works, RED is the comprehension gate failing on authoring drift), Naya 4 proposed the minimum-risk next step: **prove the cause before permanently encoding the cure** — one falsifiable backfill experiment (add the missing canonical governance keys to SN-020/021/022, rerun the workflow) before building a permanent CI conformance gate. "If that happens, the diagnosis is experimentally proven. If it does not, we stop and investigate the next failure instead of having encoded a wrong assumption into CI." Then CODA 3 found the flaw in that experiment: if the workflow derives the runtime event ID from `capture_id`, re-executing an edited capture under the same ID tests the harness's replay guard, not the diagnosis — a green result would prove nothing about the hypothesis. Naya 4 conceded and redesigned: withdraw the in-place backfill as the causal experiment; instead run **one genuinely fresh conforming capture through the four-job chain, zero runtime changes — green = diagnosis proven**. SN-020/021/022's REDs stand as honest historical evidence, never rewritten to green. CODA 1's warning makes the general law: **a gate built on an untested premise becomes a permanent wrong rule**.

Why this is brain-grade: teams routinely "validate" repairs with experiments that can only produce the answer they want. The EVENT_ID_REPLAY finding names a whole class of self-validating experiments: re-running edited evidence through a pipeline whose identity model keys off the thing you edited. The acceptance criterion for any causal experiment is therefore positional: **a green result must be possible ONLY IF the hypothesis is true**. If green is also consistent with the hypothesis being false (replay guard ate it, cache served it, the gate wasn't the binding constraint), the experiment is theater and the repair that follows it is luck. And the historical REDs stay RED — rewriting failures to green after the fact destroys the evidence trail future verification needs (SN-0080's frozen-evidence retirement said never mutate the freeze; this says the same about failure history). A cold successor that (a) runs the cheapest falsifiable experiment first, (b) checks the experiment's own machinery can't explain its result, and (c) leaves honest failures standing, never encodes a wrong assumption into CI. Cousins: SN-0245 (reproduce the failure before repairing it — the three-class evidence boundary this note extends to experiment design), SN-0066 (red before green — publish the failing case on the frozen SHA before any fix), SN-0080 (frozen-evidence retirement — retire bad freezes by explicit action, never mutate), SN-0079 (withheld certification is the gate working — the gate's hold is a terminal observation, not a failure to route around).

The team's causal experiment for the cold-recall RED was redesigned on the board: in-place backfill was withdrawn (re-running edited captures under the same ID would test the replay guard, not the diagnosis), replaced by one genuinely fresh conforming capture through the four-job chain — green = diagnosis proven, zero runtime changes. The old REDs stay RED as honest history. And the standing warning: a gate built on an untested premise becomes a permanent wrong rule — the experiment comes before the gate, always.

layers.body: There's a new rule for testing fixes. First, run the cheapest possible test of your theory — before building any permanent machinery. But here's the catch: the test must be designed so that a "pass" can *only* mean your theory was right. In this case, fixing old records and re-running them wouldn't prove anything, because the system might just notice "this is the same record I saw before" and skip the real work. So instead they send one brand-new, correctly-made record through the whole system — if it passes, the theory is proven. Old failures stay on the record; nobody rewrites history to look green.

The experiment has to be designed so a passing result can only mean the theory is right — if "pass" could also mean "the system just repeated its old answer," the test proves nothing. In this case they abandoned editing old records and re-running them (that would only test the system's replay guard), and instead sent one brand-new correct record through the whole chain. Old failures stay on the books as history; they're never painted over.

notes.title: The Runner Echoes Source — Measure the Failing Line, Never Infer It
notes.subtitle: CODA 1 read the cold-recall failure's log and concluded "retrieval succeeded and behavior changed" — citing `treatment.source_intelligent_block_id` resolving to the exact block in the log payload.…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
CODA 1 read the cold-recall failure's log and concluded "retrieval succeeded and behavior changed" — citing `treatment.source_intelligent_block_id` resolving to the exact block in the log payload. That payload was the runner echoing unevaluated script source, not runtime values: the script had died at line 49, twenty-two lines before the treatment dict was ever constructed. Two hard rules fell out of the repair. **(1) Log echo is not runtime evidence.** A line of source text printed in a log proves nothing executed; citing it as a measured outcome is inference masquerading as measurement. CODA 1's own retraction is the canonical admission: "I asserted 'line 49 = the behavior assert.' I never verified that. I inferred it from proximity to the log payload and treated the inference as measurement — exactly the error I have been flagging in others for ten days." **(2) The failing line number is positive evidence too.** Naya 4 mapped the traceback against the workflow source programmatically: line 49 was `assert comprehension["understands_raw_source_separate"]` (the conformance gate), line 71 was the behavior assert (never reached). Because execution failed *at* 49, relative line 48 — `assert comprehension["exact_current_capture_retrieved"]` — *passed*, which independently proves the exact block WAS retrieved. CODA 3 then counted heredoc-relative lines independently (opener at file line 388, body 389) and confirmed rel 48/49/50. The strongest positive evidence in the whole chain — retrieval works — came from exactly where the failure occurred.

Why this is brain-grade: the diagnosis hinged on a line number, and a line number is cheap to measure and expensive to guess. "Which assert failed?" is always answerable by counting against the source — no seat should ever infer it from proximity, log color, or payload shape. And every failing line carries its own shadow proof: everything above it in the same script executed cleanly. A cold successor that (a) counts lines programmatically, (b) treats echoed source as unread testimony, and (c) reads the failing line's position as evidence about the passing lines, gets failure location right the first time — no retraction needed. Cousins: SN-0074 (retraction discipline — SN-048 absolute downgraded by live falsification), SN-0061 (post-merge verification at the pin — verdicts die at every new SHA; here, verdicts die at every assumed line number), SN-0059 (attribute the failure before you blame the change — the same misattribution class, this time against a log), SN-0083 (retain the UNKNOWN with its missing evidence named — Naya 4's honesty note about being 401'd on the logs endpoint named exactly which leg was inferred).

CODA 1 owned the miss publicly with proof; that correction culture is what let the team converge in under an hour.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Someone read the computer's error report and said "see, the important part worked" — but they were reading the instructions the computer *would have* run, not what it actually ran. The program crashed before reaching them. The lesson: always count which exact line broke by checking the actual program file — don't guess from the report's shape. And a bonus: when you know the crash happened at line 49, you also know lines 1–48 ran fine — the crash location tells you what *did* work, not just what failed.

Before claiming anything about the error, the reader must count the exact line that broke against the actual program file, never guess from what the report looks like. There's a useful flip side: if the program broke at line 49, lines before it ran cleanly — so the failure location also tells you what was working.

notes.title: Reproduce the Failure Before Repairing It — Three-Class Evidence Boundary
notes.subtitle: When the PRIORITY ONE seam failed (cold recall RED on the last four capture merges), the judge seat did not patch it — it wrote a repair protocol. Two laws: **(1) the three-class evidence boundary**…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
When the PRIORITY ONE seam failed (cold recall RED on the last four capture merges), the judge seat did not patch it — it wrote a repair protocol. Two laws: **(1) the three-class evidence boundary** — every claim gets one of three honest labels: IMPLEMENTED-and-previously-observed (we have seen it work), TEAM-REPORTED / MUST BE REPRODUCED FROM RUN LOGS (another seat reported it; this seat has not yet independently reread the run logs — the failure class is NOT independently confirmed), NOT PROVEN (the golden lifecycle). The judge explicitly recorded that it had "independently confirmed the workflow source and the failure-sensitive rung, but I have NOT yet independently reread those four workflow run logs in this seat" — and refused to claim more. **(2) Reproduce-before-repair** — before any code changes: re-read the exact run logs, classify the failure at ONE exact seam (source registry resolution / lineage IDs / runtime verify reread / checkpoint provenance / exact-content match / machine-view comprehension / identity/authority / transport), then make the smallest repair at that seam only. No parallel distraction: freeze non-lifecycle work, keep the 3-artifact invariant, run the gate order (#1349 merge → #1350 rebase/handshake → #1351 against resulting index), repair at one seam, re-run the same capture path until all four workflow jobs are green.

Why this is brain-grade: it is the operational answer to the two most expensive failure modes in the log history — repairing the wrong seam (SN-059 family: attribute before you blame) and claiming more than a seat has verified (SN-121/083: name the boundary, retain the UNKNOWN). The three classes make under-claiming mechanical instead of heroic, and "reproduce from the exact run logs before changing code" makes a second seat's report a hypothesis, never a verdict. A cold successor that follows this protocol never edits code against a failure it has not reproduced — the most expensive kind of write. Cousins: SN-0121 (the verifier names its boundary), SN-0083 (retain the UNKNOWN with its missing evidence named), SN-0059 (clean-main control — attribute the failure before blaming the change), SN-0236 (one repair per RED class — exactly one repair owns the class).

Nobody edits code against a failure they haven't reproduced.

Only after seeing the failure themselves do they name the ONE exact spot it broke and make the smallest possible fix there — and then re-run the same test until it's green. layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:

Anything short of that is storage, not compounding intelligence.** The live evidence forced the declaration: the capture side worked, but the last four capture merges failed at the `cold-successor-held-out` rung of `live-intelligence-commit-proof.yml` — write works, RECALL FAILS. "If she can't recall it, she didn't learn it." Not before.

Why this is brain-grade: every prior capture effort (including SN-0242's canonical flow and SN-0103's process-death memory proof) specified the legs; this is the standing acceptance criterion that judges all of them. A cold successor that knows this never ships "capture complete" as done — done is the golden run: one note through every leg, recall proven, behavior changed, independently verified. notes.title: The Rich Standard — Shawn's Design Law: Black Is the Canvas, Color Is Light, Never Paint
notes.subtitle: During the Smart Spaces v2 review on 2026-10-04, Shawn stated a new design law — **THE RICH STANDARD** — that locks the visual language for every build going forward: **black is the canvas; color is…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
During the Smart Spaces v2 review on 2026-10-04, Shawn stated a new design law — **THE RICH STANDARD** — that locks the visual language for every build going forward: **black is the canvas; color is light, never paint.** Surfaces are obsidian-black; color never appears as flat fill — it lives only as edge light (borders, glows): a red room is a black room *lit red*. The palette is fixed at nine rich jewel tones (purple `#7c3aed`, indigo `#4338ca`, cyan `#0891b2`, emerald `#059669`, yellow `#eab308`, gold `#b8860b`, orange `#ea580c`, red `#dc2626`, teal `#0d9488`) — deep and dark, never pastel, never rainbow. Rest states stay calm; hover ignites (border brightens, glow blooms; touch alive, rest quiet). Contrast is law: white text on black pill with a colored edge; tone-on-tone (red-on-red) is a defect. One accent per component — never two competing colors. Jewel avatars: single initial, rich radial gradient, bright edge, glow, dynamic per member. Full-bleed rooms, no narrow columns. Alive motion: slow auto-scroll marquees with edge fade, pause on hover.

Why this is brain-grade: this law completes the design-contract lineage — it operationalizes "jewel colors are for jewels, never text fills" (the 2026-10-04 Connect-room correction) and the v1.1 color-jobs amendment (accent jewels / endless flow / fixed board colors) into a build-ready nine-point program that every seat can execute without interpretation. It is Shawn-direct, first applied in `spaces-v2.html` across 27 official spaces, and relayed to Naya 3 to be baked into the design protocol. A cold successor reading this never guesses the palette, the rest/hover contract, or the contrast rule — they build to it. NAYA NOTE carries the verbatim nine points so no relay layer can dilute them.

notes.title: The Tripwire Firing RED on Real Drift Is Correct Behavior — Classify PR-Introduced Red Before Blaming the Base
notes.subtitle: Not every CI red on a PR is inherited. When a PR itself adds a new BRAIN/ file without regenerating the governed index artifacts, the drift-check red is **REAL-PR-INTRODUCED-DRIFT** — the guardrail…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Not every CI red on a PR is inherited. When a PR itself adds a new BRAIN/ file without regenerating the governed index artifacts, the drift-check red is **REAL-PR-INTRODUCED-DRIFT** — the guardrail firing exactly as designed, on real evidence, against the change under review. The independent-verification battery on PR #1350 established this class in one tick: the PR added a BRAIN file, the index was not regenerated in-branch, the tripwire correctly went red. That verdict is the *complement* of the BASE-DEFECT class (SN-0236): same red step, opposite attribution. The discipline it demands is twofold. First, **classify before you heal** — prove which class the red belongs to (bare-pin reproduction for base-defect; changed-fileset diff for PR-introduced), and never chase green until the class is named. Second, **heal the real class, not your copy of it** — the heal sequence for real drift is merge-the-repair → rebase → regenerate the index artifacts *in the owning lane's branch*; the verifier explicitly did NOT regenerate inside #1350 because it is another lane's in-flight work and propose-first applies. Regenerating the index inside your verification or inside someone else's branch is not a fix — it is an unowned repair on a live artifact, and it teaches the wrong reflex: that a firing tripwire is a problem with the wire.

Why this is brain-grade: earlier lessons proved attribution (SN-0059: clean-main control run — attribute the failure before blaming the change; SN-0236: one repair per inherited RED class). This note closes the loop on the *other* half of every CI-red verdict: the change itself may be the drift source, and when it is, the red is the system working. A cold successor that treats every red as "the base's fault" will sleepwalk past real drift; one that treats every red as "my bug" will duplicate repairs. The rule: **name the red's source class first — PR-introduced or base-inherited — then route the heal to the class's rightful owner, and never "fix" another lane's branch silently.** The tripwire is not the enemy; an unclassified red is.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — one more CI discipline from the morning's batteries: a PR went red on the brain-index drift check, and this time the red was the guardrail doing its job — the PR itself added a new Brain file without regenerating the index, so real drift, correct red. New rule: every CI red gets classified first — did the change introduce the drift, or did it inherit it from the base? Same red, opposite causes, opposite heals. The verifier named the class, proposed the heal sequence, and did not touch the other lane's branch. That's the discipline I'm banking: name the source before you chase the green.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a smoke alarm. It can go off because the house is smoky (the base was already bad) — or because you burned toast (your change made the smoke). A PR made the CI test go red, but the "alarm" was right: the PR itself added a file and forgot to update the index — it burned its own toast. New rule: before fixing anything, figure out WHO made the smoke. If it's your toast, clean it up in your own kitchen — don't reach into someone else's.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: One of our proposals failed an automatic check — but the check was right. The proposal itself had added a new file without updating the register, so the failure was genuine. The rule we've learned: when an automatic check fails, first find out whether the failure came from the new work or from what was already there. Fix it in the right place — and never quietly "fix" someone else's work; propose it instead.
